records.source_title: Wish You Were Here? The Economic Impact of the Tourism Shutdown from Australia's 2019-20 Black Summer Bushfires
records.author_or_outlet: Reiner, Malik, Lenzen; Economics of Disasters and Climate Change
records.mechanism: Fire and smoke cut visitor numbers, so tourism firms lose turnover and shed staff; the loss then travels up the supply chain to suppliers in other places (spillover) -> IL
records.affected_group: Tourism businesses, their workers and suppliers
records.quant_evidence: A$2.8b total output loss (61% more than direct loss of A$1.7b); about 7,300 jobs lost nationally, 3,171 in NSW

records.source_title: Wish You Were Here? (tourism supply-chain study)
records.author_or_outlet: Reiner, Malik, Lenzen; Economics of Disasters and Climate Change
records.mechanism: Input-output linkages mean job and output losses show up in states and sectors far from the fire, so council-level burned area understates the economic hit (input-output method, so a modelled not observed result)
records.affected_group: Workers and firms in supplier industries outside burned areas
records.quant_evidence: Jobs lost spread across all states: NSW 3,171, Qld 1,499, Vic 1,430, SA 516, WA 479

records.source_title: Wildfire Exposure, Impact, and Recovery: climate inequality lessons from Australia's Black Summer (income, housing, unpaid work)
records.author_or_outlet: Akter and Grafton (research reported via PreventionWeb)
records.place: Australia (burned small areas, ~400 people each, matched to unburned, Census 2016 vs 2021)
records.mechanism: Communities with the most severe burn saw weekly personal income fall relative to matched unburned areas, linked to local work and business disruption -> SL/IL
records.affected_group: Residents of high-burn-severity communities, especially low-income
records.quant_evidence: Largest falls in average weekly personal income in highest-severity areas (exact dollar values not seen)

records.source_title: Wildfire Exposure, Impact, and Recovery (Akter and Grafton)
records.mechanism: Housing lost or damaged and slow rebuilding push up rents and overcrowding in low-income neighbourhoods; underinsurance and pandemic supply-chain delays slow rebuilding -> SL (housing/displacement)
records.quant_evidence: Rising rents and overcrowding reported in low-income areas (no figure seen)

records.source_title: Wildfire Exposure, Impact, and Recovery (Akter and Grafton)
records.mechanism: Cleanup, caring and household recovery work falls more on women, raising unpaid domestic work and cutting time for paid work -> SL (unpaid recovery work)
records.quant_evidence: Higher unpaid domestic work for women in burned areas (no figure seen)

records.source_title: Black Saturday bushfires: counting the cost
records.author_or_outlet: Ulubasoglu and Beaini; Australian Journal of Emergency Management
records.mechanism: Local business damage and job disruption reduce personal income for residents of disaster areas; losses concentrated in agriculture, retail and tourism -> IL/SL
records.quant_evidence: Average ~10% income loss vs matched non-exposed area; agriculture -31%, retail -13%, tourism -12%

records.source_title: Black Saturday bushfires: counting the cost
records.mechanism: Existing disadvantage amplifies losses: low earners, women and renters have less buffer and flexibility -> SL (vulnerable groups)
records.quant_evidence: Low-income -18%, women -14% vs men -9%, renters -14%

records.source_title: Black Saturday bushfires: counting the cost
records.mechanism: People who move out of the disaster zone pay a job-and-occupation mobility cost: lose local networks and fitted work -> IL/SL
records.quant_evidence: Relocators had about 19% income decline

records.source_title: Black Saturday bushfires: counting the cost
records.mechanism: Disaster-driven demand for health services raises overtime and pay for health workers (a winner group) -> IL (sectoral winners)
records.quant_evidence: +8% income for healthcare workers

records.source_title: Black Saturday bushfires: counting the cost
records.mechanism: Lost income and weaker finances feed through to worse mental health (income as a channel from IL to SL)
records.quant_evidence: Authors report reduced incomes and financial capability as critical factors in worse mental health (no coefficient seen)

records.source_title: The unequal burden of disasters in Australia
records.author_or_outlet: Ulubasoglu; Australian Journal of Emergency Management
records.mechanism: Disasters widen the income gap: insecure and low-income workers lose, middle and high earners often hold or gain -> SL
records.affected_group: Low-income earners, small business owners, part-time workers
records.quant_evidence: Agricultural workers lost about A$8,000/yr for two years; accommodation/food workers about A$5,000; low-vs-middle income gap rose about A$7,000/yr after Qld floods

records.source_title: The unequal burden of disasters in Australia
records.mechanism: Recovery money is allocated mainly to business and infrastructure rather than household income support, so who receives it shapes who recovers -> FP (who pays / grants)
records.quant_evidence: Only about 10% of recovery spending went to income/wage help, about 80% to businesses

records.source_title: Beyond Bushfires: Community, Resilience and Recovery (10-year report)
records.author_or_outlet: Gibbs et al., University of Melbourne
records.mechanism: Trauma, loss and stress produce mental ill-health that stays high for years; social support and community ties help recovery -> SL (mental health)
records.quant_evidence: About 62.6% felt personally recovered at 10 years (so roughly a third did not); 1,017 people at wave 1, 525 at 10 years

records.source_title: Catastrophic fires, human displacement, and real estate prices in California
records.author_or_outlet: Hennighausen and James; Journal of Housing Economics
records.mechanism: Mass loss of housing pushes displaced people into nearby markets and bids up prices and rents in surrounding towns (displacement -> housing cost) -> SL
records.affected_group: Renters and buyers in surrounding communities
records.quant_evidence: Prices in nearby areas rose about 13% in six weeks (within 25 miles), effect persistent about 10 months; insignificant beyond about 100 miles

records.source_title: Disaster recovery gentrification in post-wildfire landscapes: the case of Paradise, CA
records.author_or_outlet: UCLA Lewis Center for Regional Policy Studies (research summary)
records.mechanism: Federal recovery aid helped advantaged residents and new buyers return and rebuild while barriers kept socially vulnerable long-term residents out, so aid design decides who gets the recovered housing -> FP/SL
records.quant_evidence: Over US$1b federal aid; no per-group figure seen

records.source_title: The Economic Impact of Hurricane Katrina on Its Victims: Evidence from Individual Tax Returns
records.author_or_outlet: Deryugina, Kawano and Levitt; AEJ: Applied Economics
records.mechanism: Displacement strongly changes where people live but income effects are small and temporary; wage income, employment and total income recover within a few years -> IL/SL
records.quant_evidence: Large persistent change in location; small, mostly transitory effects on wages and employment; incomes recovered and passed controls within a few years

records.source_title: The Local Labor Market Impacts of US Megafires
records.mechanism: Megafires reduce local employment and wage earnings in the flame zone through business and workplace disruption -> IL
records.quant_evidence: Significantly lower per capita wage earnings for up to about two years after the fire (size not seen)

records.source_title: Fires and Local Labor Markets
records.mechanism: Fires shift jobs between sectors: tourism-related jobs fall while construction and real-estate services rise -> IL (sectoral winners and losers)
records.quant_evidence: Not seen in detail; summary only

records.source_title: Air Pollution and the Labor Market: Evidence from Wildfire Smoke
records.author_or_outlet: Borgschulte, Molitor and Zou; Review of Economics and Statistics
records.mechanism: Smoke exposure cuts hours, health and productivity, so earnings and some employment fall, even far from the fire -> IL via smoke
records.affected_group: Workers, especially in outdoor and exposed jobs
records.quant_evidence: Each extra smoke day lowers quarterly earnings about 0.1%; employment exits explain about 13% of the loss

records.source_title: Domestic violence increases during disasters (review of Australian evidence)
records.author_or_outlet: Flinders University review of 39 papers; PreventionWeb summary
records.mechanism: Stress, financial strain and male insecurity after disaster raise violence while services are stretched on recovery; victims struggle to get support -> SL (domestic violence)
records.quant_evidence: Women in worst-affected Black Saturday regions reported intimate partner violence at about 7 times the rate in less-affected communities

records.source_title: Unprecedented smoke-related health burden associated with the 2019-20 bushfires in eastern Australia
records.author_or_outlet: Borchers Arriagada et al.; Medical Journal of Australia
records.mechanism: Smoke causes deaths, hospital admissions and emergency visits, creating large health-system costs far from the fire front -> SL (health) and FP (health spend)
records.quant_evidence: 417 excess deaths; 1,124 cardiovascular and 2,027 respiratory hospitalisations; 1,305 asthma ED visits; about A$1.95b health cost (NSW A$1.07b)

records.source_title: House and contents underinsurance: insights from bushfire-prone Australia
records.author_or_outlet: Booth et al.; International Journal of Disaster Risk Reduction
records.mechanism: Households are underinsured at household, landscape and market level, so a fire loss becomes the household's own debt or lost wealth -> SL (and DL not covered)
records.affected_group: Households in bushfire-prone areas, especially lower income
records.quant_evidence: Qualitative; BAL rules can add 20% or more to rebuild cost

records.source_title: Coverage neglect in homeowners insurance (Marshall Fire study)
records.author_or_outlet: University of Colorado Boulder researchers; reported by Yahoo Finance
records.mechanism: Homeowners accept insurer-suggested cover that is below rebuild cost, so they cannot rebuild and fall behind in recovery -> SL/FP (reconstruction gap)
records.quant_evidence: 74% underinsured; average gap about US$139,000; underinsured owners 25% less likely to apply for rebuild permit within a year

records.source_title: The Fiscal Impacts of Wildfires on California Municipalities
records.author_or_outlet: Liao and Kousky; Journal of the Association of Environmental and Resource Economists
records.mechanism: Fires raise both council revenue (property and sales tax) and spending (safety, community development); the net is a budget shortfall -> FP
records.quant_evidence: Deficit probability up 25 percentage points; excess revenue down US$97 per person (10.7% of budget); property tax +21.2% over 5 years

records.source_title: The Fiscal Impacts of Wildfires on California Municipalities
records.mechanism: Rate-base effect: population leaves only slightly, but California rules cap property reassessment, so revenue effects depend on tax rules -> FP (rate base)
records.quant_evidence: Population down only 0.78% in 5 years

records.source_title: Effects of the Fort McMurray wildfires on the health of evacuated workers: follow-up of 2 cohorts
records.mechanism: Evacuated workers lose work and income, and depression scores are higher with financial loss from lack of work (job loss -> mental health)
records.quant_evidence: 129 workers; 33.9% had health issues soon after, 10.1% at 102 days; about one in four not back in paid work at follow-up; over half had income loss

records.source_title: Household Finance after a Natural Disaster: The Case of Hurricane Katrina
records.author_or_outlet: Gallagher and Hartley; AEJ: Economic Policy
records.mechanism: Insurance payouts let flooded homeowners repay mortgages instead of rebuilding, so debt falls while credit stress is small and brief -> SL/debt
records.quant_evidence: Credit-card and delinquency spikes modest and short-lived; larger drops in total debt where flooding was worse; about US$6.7b insurance claims paid

records.source_title: Let the Rich Be Flooded: The Distribution of Financial Aid and Distress after Hurricane Harvey
records.mechanism: Credit-constrained uninsured households fall into delinquency and bankruptcy after flood loss; insurance protects those inside floodplain -> SL (debt)
records.quant_evidence: About 20% rise in bankruptcies and 13% rise in severely delinquent debt share for such homeowners in flooded blocks

records.source_title: Let the Rich Be Flooded (Harvey aid)
records.mechanism: Government disaster loans and grants were allocated regressively, so aid did not offset starting inequality -> FP (who gets grants)
records.quant_evidence: SBA loans and FEMA grants found regressive in allocation (no single number)

records.source_title: The black summer bushfires: impacts and risk factors for livestock bushfire injury in south-eastern Australia
records.author_or_outlet: Cowled et al.; Australian Veterinary Journal
records.mechanism: Fire kills or forces destruction of livestock, removing farm capital and income, with higher losses for mixed beef-sheep farms -> DL (livestock) and IL (farm income)
records.quant_evidence: Over 56,000 livestock killed or euthanised (up to about 69,000); 46% of 46 farms had losses; median 20% of stock on affected farms

records.source_title: Wildfire smoke exposure hurts learning outcomes (Nature Sustainability study)
records.author_or_outlet: Stanford news summary of Nature Sustainability paper
records.mechanism: Smoke exposure during school days lowers test scores (absences, asthma, cognition) and may lower later earnings -> SL (education)
records.affected_group: Children, especially younger and in disadvantaged communities
records.quant_evidence: About 11,700 districts over 8 years; effect nearly doubles with heavy smoke on school days

records.source_title: Effects of wildfire-caused school closures (California)
records.mechanism: Wildfires close schools, causing learning loss, worst for young pupils -> SL (education)
records.quant_evidence: About 34,000 school-closure days across 6,664 schools in 17 years; wildfire caused about two-thirds of unplanned closures

records.source_title: Assessing the social context of wildfire-affected areas: the case of mainland Portugal
records.mechanism: Parishes with more burned area are older, less populated, with poorer housing and higher unemployment, so fire risk and fire loss concentrate on already vulnerable places (vulnerability moderator, direction fire to socioeconomics unclear)

records.source_title: Wildfires and Real Estate Values in California
records.author_or_outlet: Bengali, Nechio and Stewart; Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco
records.mechanism: Closeness to past fire zones lowers home values as buyers re-price risk (property values) -> SL/FP (rate base)
records.quant_evidence: 2018-2021: homes farther from past fires about 2% higher value; no clear effect 2008-2017; insurance does little to offset

records.source_title: The Fiscal Cost of Hurricanes: Disaster Aid versus Social Insurance
records.mechanism: Disasters raise ordinary transfers (unemployment insurance, medical payments) for a decade, far above visible disaster aid; the hidden government cost is bigger than reported -> FP
records.quant_evidence: Fiscal cost per person rises from about US$150 to at least US$780 when transfers included

records.source_title: Taken by Storm: Business Financing and Survival in the Aftermath of Hurricane Katrina
records.author_or_outlet: Basker and Miranda; Journal of Economic Geography
records.mechanism: Physically damaged small firms with financing limits often fail rather than reopen, so closures exceed what damage alone predicts -> IL (closures) and DL (premises)
records.quant_evidence: Low survival of damaged firms, worst for small firms (no single rate seen)

records.source_title: Storms and Jobs: The Effect of Hurricanes on Individuals' Employment and Earnings over the Long Term
records.author_or_outlet: Groen, Kutzbach and Polivka; Journal of Labor Economics
records.mechanism: Job separations cause short-run earnings loss, strongest when home or workplace was damaged; later gains from higher local wages in rebuilding sectors -> IL (spillover and winners)
records.affected_group: Workers in storm areas; rebuilding-sector workers gain
records.quant_evidence: Modest negative earnings effect in year one, positive from year three

records.source_title: After the Fires: wellbeing of Australian emergency services personnel after Black Summer
records.mechanism: Responders face life-threat exposure and long deployment, raising PTSD, distress and suicidality -> SL (health of responders)
records.affected_group: Fire and emergency volunteers and employees
records.quant_evidence: 4,000+ personnel; 31% of volunteers felt life at risk; probable PTSD/distress 4.2% volunteers and 7.3% employees two years on

records.source_title: Value beyond money: Australia's special dependence on volunteer firefighters
records.author_or_outlet: Western Sydney University (university news piece, not peer-reviewed)
records.mechanism: Volunteers who are self-employed or work for small firms lose income while fighting fires for weeks, an unpaid recovery and response cost -> IL/SL (unpaid work)
records.quant_evidence: About 64,500 of 82,480 responders were volunteers; volunteer value about A$1.3b

records.source_title: Health impacts of smoke from Australia's Black Summer bushfires revealed (ANU survey, Frontiers in Public Health)
records.mechanism: Smoke and evacuation disrupt sleep, routines, work and social ties, causing physical symptoms and poor mental health well beyond burned areas -> SL
records.quant_evidence: 2,084 adults surveyed; 97% reported at least one smoke symptom; about 60% directly impacted

records.source_title: The 2020 special report of the MJA-Lancet Countdown on health and climate change: lessons learnt from Australia's Black Summer
records.mechanism: Insured losses and health costs of a mega-season show who pays: insurers, public health system, households -> FP/DL
records.quant_evidence: Insured economic losses about A$2.2b

records.source_title: Inter-regional economic impact of the reduction in tourism following the Maui wildfires
records.author_or_outlet: UHERO, University of Hawaii (institute analysis, not peer-reviewed)
records.mechanism: Visitor drop plus destroyed businesses cause jobs and unemployment spikes in the host island and losses in other islands through supply links -> IL
records.quant_evidence: About 18,000 jobs lost Sep-Dec 2023, about half through 2024; statewide 23,100 FTE jobs and US$2.3b output; up to 28% of loss outside Maui; unemployment claims 130/week to 4,449 in week two

records.source_title: Wine industry's black summer as cost of smoke taint, burnt vineyards and lost sales add up
records.author_or_outlet: ABC News (news item) plus Beverages (MDPI) review on smoke taint
records.mechanism: Smoke taints grapes and wine, causing crop rejection and lost sales; wine tourism also drops -> IL (farm income, tourism)
records.quant_evidence: Industry estimate about A$40m (NSW association up to A$100m with tourism); reported up to A$150m grapes needlessly discarded

records.source_title: UCLA study of renter outcomes after the January 2025 Los Angeles wildfires
records.author_or_outlet: UCLA Lewis Center (research report, not peer-reviewed)
records.mechanism: Housing loss and demand surge raise rents and leave renters worse off than owners (renters lack insurance on structures and have fewer rebuild rights) -> SL (housing)
records.quant_evidence: Survey of over 2,300 residents; rents up about 20% county-wide, up to 130% in some neighbourhoods

records.source_title: Black Saturday cost victims A$52,300 in psychological damage (coverage of Deakin/Beyond Bushfires economics)
records.mechanism: Psychological harm carries a large per-person cost that is not in standard damage tallies -> SL (valuation of mental health)
records.quant_evidence: A$52,300 per victim in the headline (method not checked)

records.source_title: Black Saturday analysis of likely cost of recent Qld and NSW fires (Deakin)
records.mechanism: Lost income and mental-health costs are a large share of total fire cost beyond property damage -> IL/SL
records.quant_evidence: Average ~10% income loss vs comparison regions

records.source_title: Australia Bushfires: the real estate perspective (Canberra 2003 and other fires)
records.mechanism: After the fire, rebuilding lifts building values and activity, so local output and house prices recover and even rise in the years after -> IL (reconstruction boom)
records.quant_evidence: GRP rose in 1-3 years after; house price index kept rising beyond two years

records.source_title: Bushfire recovery chapter, ACT Budget 2003-04 (Canberra 2003 net government cost)
records.mechanism: Government carries recovery spending and lost revenue, so net cost lands on the budget over several years -> FP
records.quant_evidence: Net cost to general government about A$121.4m over five years; total damage over A$300m including about A$50m forests

records.source_title: Recovering from the 2003 Canberra bushfire: a work in progress
records.mechanism: Medium-to-long recovery is a slow personal and community process, with rebuilding delays and stress years after (rebuilding gap) -> SL

records.source_title: Power and telecommunications outages in Black Summer (Telstra NSW Bushfire Inquiry submission and local reporting)
records.author_or_outlet: Telstra submission to NSW Bushfire Inquiry (government/inquiry document)
records.mechanism: Power cuts, not fire damage, caused most phone-tower outages; towns lose EFTPOS, phones and radio, stopping trade and slowing recovery -> IL (infrastructure outage)
records.affected_group: Businesses and residents in cut-off towns
records.quant_evidence: 1,406 telecom facilities impacted (818 in NSW); direct fire damage only about 1% of outage incidents; over 100,000 people without power, some for weeks

records.source_title: Regional council disaster costs (Productivity Commission disaster funding inquiry submissions)
records.author_or_outlet: Local council submissions to the Productivity Commission
records.mechanism: Councils face large disaster costs relative to revenue and fear cost-shifting from higher governments, so money for roads, rates and services is crowded out -> FP (who pays, opportunity cost)
records.affected_group: Rural and regional councils and ratepayers
records.quant_evidence: Lockyer Valley: A$42.5m in 2011 = 88% of annual revenue base; Swan Hill: over A$600,000 net ratepayer cost over five years

records.source_title: Fort McMurray population-based survey of psychological symptoms one year after the fire
records.author_or_outlet: Fort McMurray evacuee survey (1,510 evacuees); article listed in search results, authors not confirmed
records.mechanism: Evacuation and loss cause high rates of PTSD, depression, anxiety and sleep problems a year later -> SL (mental health)
records.quant_evidence: 1,510 evacuees interviewed May-July 2017 (rates not seen)

records.source_title: Special report: Update to the economic costs of natural disasters in Australia
records.author_or_outlet: Deloitte Access Economics for Australian Business Roundtable for Disaster Resilience & Safer Communities
records.mechanism: Property and public-asset damage triggers extra financial costs on top of the damage itself (clean-up, emergency response, evacuation, temporary housing, public-asset repair), so the true bill is a multiple of insured damage
records.quant_evidence: A$38bn/yr average cost today, rising to A$73bn/yr by 2060 (low-emissions scenario)

records.source_title: Special report: Update to the economic costs of natural disasters in Australia
records.author_or_outlet: Deloitte Access Economics for Australian Business Roundtable
records.mechanism: Disasters raise mental health problems, high-risk alcohol and drug use, worsening of chronic illness, injuries and family violence, which are priced as social costs added to the economic bill
records.quant_evidence: Social costs = 37% (A$195bn over 40 yrs) of total flood costs under low-emissions scenario (floods, not bushfire-specific)

records.source_title: Special report: Update to the economic costs of natural disasters in Australia
records.author_or_outlet: Deloitte Access Economics for Australian Business Roundtable
records.mechanism: Permanent unemployment, education disruption, loss of social cohesion and higher crime are named as real social costs but are NOT measured because data are missing

records.source_title: Special report: Update to the economic costs of natural disasters in Australia
records.author_or_outlet: Deloitte Access Economics for Australian Business Roundtable
records.mechanism: Short-term local tourism and supply-chain losses are left out of national cost totals because spending may simply move to another region or time, so local damage is bigger than the national net loss (a 'who loses locally vs nationally' issue)
records.affected_group: tourism operators and suppliers in affected region

records.source_title: Update to the economic costs of natural disasters in Australia: Methodology paper
records.author_or_outlet: Deloitte Access Economics for Australian Business Roundtable
records.disaster: Black Saturday 2009 and other reference events
records.mechanism: Flow-on financial and social costs are estimated as a fixed multiple of asset damage, calibrated on Black Saturday, SE Queensland floods 2010-11 and the 2007 Pasha Bulker storm; this assumes the multiple is constant across event sizes

records.source_title: Natural Disaster Funding Arrangements, Inquiry Report No. 74 (Vol. 1)
records.mechanism: Cost shifting: federal reimbursement of state/local recovery spending (NDRRA) weakens the incentive for states and councils to mitigate or insure, so the burden shifts up to the Commonwealth and later back to taxpayers
records.affected_group: state and local governments, Commonwealth budget
records.quant_evidence: Commonwealth paid up to 75% of state recovery costs above thresholds; Commission proposed 50% share

records.source_title: Natural Disaster Funding Arrangements, Inquiry Report No. 74 (Vol. 1)
records.mechanism: Opportunity cost / crowd-out: governments pour money into post-disaster reconstruction and under-invest in mitigation, so recovery spending displaces cheaper prevention spending
records.quant_evidence: Commonwealth mitigation spending only about 3% of its post-disaster spending; over A$8bn spent post-disaster

records.source_title: Natural Disaster Funding Arrangements, Inquiry Report No. 74 (Vol. 1)
records.mechanism: Reimbursement-style funding makes councils spend on eligible items (e.g. asset restoration) and under-spend on non-eligible activities; recovery bills become a growing unfunded liability for governments

records.source_title: Natural Disaster Funding Arrangements, Inquiry Report No. 74 (Vol. 1)
records.mechanism: Disasters impose direct market costs (property, infrastructure), indirect market costs (disrupted activity) and non-market costs (deaths, wellbeing); data exist mainly for direct costs, so indirect and social losses are poorly measured
records.quant_evidence: Insurance losses >A$21bn 1970-2013; 10% of events = 80% of insured losses

records.source_title: Natural Disaster Funding Arrangements, Inquiry Report No. 74 (Vol. 1)
records.mechanism: Insurance stamp duty and taxes raise premiums, which can lead to non-insurance or underinsurance, leaving households and businesses to bear uninsured losses after a disaster

records.source_title: Australian bushfires 2019-20: exploring the short-term health impacts
records.author_or_outlet: Australian Institute of Health and Welfare (AIHW)
records.mechanism: Smoke pollution raises emergency department visits for respiratory problems and demand for asthma/shortness-of-breath inhalers, adding health-system cost and lost activity
records.affected_group: residents of smoke-affected regions, people with asthma/lung disease
records.quant_evidence: NSW ED respiratory visits up by as much as 50% in some areas vs previous summer; inhaler sales up about 70% in Coffs Harbour-Grafton region in one week of Nov 2019 (secondary summary of AIHW)

records.source_title: Australian bushfires 2019-20: exploring the short-term health impacts
records.mechanism: Fire exposure raises use of mental health services and GP visits in fire-affected regions; AIHW notes psychological effects may last for years

records.source_title: Data update: health impacts of the 2019-20 bushfires
records.mechanism: Smoke makes people stay indoors and cut outdoor activity (exercise), and active fire zones drive burn-injury hospitalisations

records.source_title: Statement on Monetary Policy Feb 2020, Box B: Macroeconomic effects of the drought and bushfires
records.mechanism: Fire and smoke cut domestic tourism spending in affected regions and deter overseas visitors, lowering regional consumption and national GDP growth for about two quarters
records.quant_evidence: GDP growth about 0.2 percentage points lower across Dec 2019 and Mar 2020 quarters

records.source_title: Statement on Monetary Policy Feb 2020, Box B
records.mechanism: Fire damage to roads, power and telecom assets and interstate transmission lines disrupts rural exports, delays transport (food prices up briefly) and briefly spikes NSW wholesale electricity prices

records.source_title: Statement on Monetary Policy Feb 2020, Box B
records.mechanism: Rebuilding spending, insurance payouts and government assistance partly offset the fall in output, so the rebuilding sector gains while regional tourism loses; RBA expected the GDP dip to be broadly offset by end-2020
records.affected_group: construction/building trades, insurers vs tourism operators

records.source_title: Statement on Monetary Policy Feb 2020, Box B
records.mechanism: Higher perceived fire risk is expected to push insurance premiums up after the event, while local accommodation prices fall

records.source_title: Retail turnover falls 0.3 per cent in January (Retail Trade, Jan 2020)
records.mechanism: Fire and smoke cut customer numbers and interrupted trading hours, so shops, cafes and department stores lose turnover in the month; food retailing rose slightly (stocking up)
records.quant_evidence: Retail -0.3% in Jan 2020; department stores -2.2%, household goods -1.1%, cafes/restaurants -0.3%, food +0.4%; ACT -2.3%

records.source_title: Labour Force, Australia, Detailed (Feb 2020) - bushfire notes
records.place: NSW Capital Region, Southern Highlands-Shoalhaven, Mid North Coast; Vic Latrobe-Gippsland
records.mechanism: Bushfires physically stopped ABS survey collection in some regions in Jan-Feb 2020, so fine-scale employment data for the worst-hit areas are missing (a data gap, no visible effect on national jobs numbers)
records.quant_evidence: Areas not surveyed in Jan 2020 were about 3.3% of NSW sample; national unemployment stayed 5.1-5.3% Jan-Mar 2020 (from search summary)

records.source_title: Northern Australia Insurance Inquiry final report
records.mechanism: Insurers price risk by individual address, so premiums jump for high-risk homes; high premiums push households to under-insure or not insure, leaving them exposed after a disaster
records.affected_group: households in high-risk areas, low-income owners
records.quant_evidence: Premiums considerably higher and rising faster than rest of Australia; monthly-payment surcharges up to 20%; 38 recommendations

records.source_title: Northern Australia Insurance Inquiry final report
records.mechanism: State stamp duty on premiums raises the cost of cover and gives state governments windfall revenue, shifting cost onto policyholders

records.source_title: Mental health, wellbeing and resilience after the 2019-20 bushfires: National Bushfire Health and Wellbeing Survey (summary)
records.author_or_outlet: Australian National University (Phoenix Australia / ANU) for the Australian Government
records.mechanism: Higher fire exposure leads to more depression, anxiety, stress and PTSD symptoms 1-1.5 years later, which can reduce capacity to work and cope
records.affected_group: directly affected adults, men with high exposure
records.quant_evidence: 1 in 5 high-exposure people at clinical cut-off for PTSD; affected men had PTSD symptoms about double the national rate

records.source_title: Mental health, wellbeing and resilience after the 2019-20 bushfires (summary)
records.mechanism: Parents affected by fire report more behavioural and emotional problems in their children, so household stress spills to children's wellbeing and schooling

records.source_title: Mental health, wellbeing and resilience after the 2019-20 bushfires (summary)
records.mechanism: Distress is not limited to people at the fire front: people living elsewhere suffer distress through financial loss linked to the fires (a spillover to indirectly affected people)
records.affected_group: indirectly affected people, incl. those outside fire postcodes
records.quant_evidence: Almost three-quarters of indirectly affected respondents showed anxiety symptoms up to two years after

records.source_title: Mental health, wellbeing and resilience after the 2019-20 bushfires (summary)
records.mechanism: Distress was especially high among Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, particularly women, so existing disadvantage compounds disaster harm
records.affected_group: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, especially women

records.source_title: Mental health, wellbeing and resilience after the 2019-20 bushfires (summary)
records.mechanism: Strong social group memberships help directly affected people keep community ties and recover; many people show resilience or growth
records.quant_evidence: Almost 80% reported some resilience; about two-thirds of disaster-affected return to pre-disaster wellbeing

records.source_title: Bushfire Recovery Programs: process and interim outcome evaluations
records.author_or_outlet: NSW Department of Regional NSW (Regional Programs)
records.mechanism: Government recovery funding (grants to councils, businesses and supply chains) is paid via reimbursement-style grants; these create disproportionate cash-flow burdens on small businesses that must front costs
records.quant_evidence: BLER Stage 2: A$283m across 195 projects; BIRP Stream 2: A$73m to 52 projects

records.source_title: Bushfire Recovery Programs: process and interim outcome evaluations
records.mechanism: Scale of government recovery spending is very large and co-funded Commonwealth/NSW; money spent here is money not spent elsewhere (opportunity cost), and delays from grant processes plus COVID/floods slowed outcomes
records.quant_evidence: A$4.4bn recovery programs (NSW share A$3bn); 2,448 homes destroyed, 26 lives lost, 5.5m ha burnt

records.source_title: Bushfire Recovery Programs: process and interim outcome evaluations
records.mechanism: Flexible small grants (BCRRF) let councils fund quick local recovery projects; but councils must also manage funding deeds, reporting and delivery, adding administrative load
records.quant_evidence: 49 councils eligible; 46 applied for BCRRF Phase 1

records.source_title: Performance audit: Bushfire recovery grants
records.mechanism: Grant allocation lacked transparency and consistency, and a A$1m minimum project threshold set at the request of a minister's office meant who got recovery money depended on process and politics, not only on need
records.quant_evidence: BLER program A$541.8m; A$1m threshold; audit made 5 recommendations

records.source_title: NSW bushfire recovery grant scheme heavily criticised by auditor
records.author_or_outlet: The Mandarin (reporting Audit Office of NSW)
records.mechanism: Directive from the Deputy Premier's office led electorates held by one party to miss out on recovery money, an example of political allocation of recovery funds (who gets grants)
records.quant_evidence: A$541.8m BLER program

records.source_title: The 2019-2020 Australian bushfires: from temporary evacuation to longer-term displacement
records.mechanism: Home destruction forces displaced households into rental housing or into friends' homes; a year of renting costs about A$19.5-23k per household, a big burden on top of rebuilding
records.quant_evidence: Rent about A$375/wk regional, A$445/wk metro (Mar 2020); A$61-72m/yr if one household per destroyed house; 64,579 new displacements recorded

records.source_title: The 2019-2020 Australian bushfires: from temporary evacuation to longer-term displacement
records.mechanism: Underinsurance plus rising rebuilding costs and builder/material shortages stretch rebuilds, prolonging displacement and sometimes forcing people to relocate away
records.quant_evidence: Rebuilds can take 3-4 years; ICA said up to 80% of insured homeowners may be underinsured; fire-standard building rules can add about 20% to rebuild cost

records.source_title: The 2019-2020 Australian bushfires: from temporary evacuation to longer-term displacement
records.mechanism: Evacuation keeps workers from their jobs; the longer people are away from home, the more work is disrupted
records.quant_evidence: Among those away more than one night, 55% said leaving home reduced their ability to work as usual vs 37% not

records.source_title: The 2019-2020 Australian bushfires: from temporary evacuation to longer-term displacement
records.mechanism: Evacuation centres and displacement expose women at risk of domestic violence to former partners and cut them off from family support, heightening family-violence risk
records.affected_group: women, especially those at risk of domestic violence

records.source_title: The 2019-2020 Australian bushfires: from temporary evacuation to longer-term displacement
records.mechanism: Charities and governments pay emergency grants, rental bonds and re-establishment grants to displaced households, easing but not eliminating the financial hit
records.quant_evidence: Red Cross paid over A$119m emergency grants to 4,380 people

records.source_title: Black Summer bushfires, NSW 2019-20 (Australian Disaster Resilience Knowledge Hub)
records.mechanism: Direct destruction of homes, facilities and outbuildings, plus livestock loss on drought-hit farms, creates the direct-loss base for later economic and social effects
records.quant_evidence: 2,448 homes and 284 facilities destroyed, 5,469 outbuildings; 1,013 homes damaged; 5.5m ha (6.2% of NSW); 26 deaths; A$1.88bn NSW insurance cost (81% of national)

records.source_title: Black Summer bushfires, NSW 2019-20 (AIDR)
records.mechanism: Commonwealth set up a large national recovery fund, so recovery is financed by federal money (cost shared with states)
records.quant_evidence: A$2bn National Bushfire Recovery Fund

records.source_title: Insured bushfire losses rise to A$1.9bn (ICA estimates)
records.author_or_outlet: Reinsurance News (reporting Insurance Council of Australia)
records.mechanism: Insurers pay claims for destroyed buildings, shifting part of the loss from households to the insurance sector (and then to premiums); the insured share is only a fraction of total loss
records.quant_evidence: Early estimate A$1.9bn, 23,362 claims; later totals 38,181 claims and A$2.32bn (ICA via search summary)

records.source_title: Australian Tourism in 2020
records.place: NSW South Coast, Vic High Country, SA Kangaroo Island, ACT
records.mechanism: Fires during peak holiday season cut domestic visitor spend in fire-hit tourism regions, with big differences by region depending on fire duration, timing and alternatives
records.affected_group: regional tourism/hospitality businesses and their workers
records.quant_evidence: March quarter 2020 visitor spend vs 2019: South Coast NSW -23% (A$251m), High Country Vic -29% (A$89m), Kangaroo Island -13%, Canberra -10%, Central Coast -7%, Blue Mountains -2%

records.source_title: Australian Tourism in 2020
records.mechanism: International visitor demand did not fall immediately (trips booked ahead, visitors go to capital cities), so the loss fell on domestic regional tourism, while some regions gained (Lakes Vic +13%, Adelaide Hills +14%)
records.quant_evidence: 1.8m international arrivals Dec 2019-Jan 2020, up 3%; 93% of international tourists visit capital cities vs 33% regions

records.source_title: Australian Tourism in 2020
records.mechanism: Government targeted tourism recovery funds after the fires (marketing, grants) to rebuild demand
records.quant_evidence: A$76m allocated for bushfire recovery in tourism

records.source_title: 2019-20 Bushfires Quick Guide, Research Note No. 1
records.author_or_outlet: Parliament of Victoria, Parliamentary Library & Information Service
records.mechanism: Tourism and agriculture lose income during the fires; early estimates put tourism losses in the billions
records.quant_evidence: Tourism reportedly lost about A$2bn with further A$4.5bn projected; ICA early loss estimate A$1.65bn (Jan 2020)

records.source_title: 2019-20 Bushfires Quick Guide, Research Note No. 1
records.mechanism: Government support packages cover clean-up, mental health services, farmer grants, income payments to volunteer firefighters and concessions, shifting recovery costs onto budgets
records.quant_evidence: A$2bn federal national bushfire recovery fund; A$100m farmer grants; A$76m mental health; A$75m clean-up (joint with Vic); Vic A$86m community recovery package

records.source_title: 2019-20 Bushfires Quick Guide, Research Note No. 1
records.mechanism: Public donations flow through charities but only a fraction reaches victims quickly, so private giving does not instantly replace lost income
records.quant_evidence: About A$500m donated by Jan 2020 (media-reported figure cited in note)

records.source_title: The impact of bushfires on student wellbeing and student learning
records.mechanism: Fires block access to school, damage facilities, make teachers unavailable and force some students to move schools; trauma harms concentration and memory and can cause lasting academic impairment
records.affected_group: school students, especially those with prior disadvantage
records.quant_evidence: About 600 NSW schools closed in late 2019 (media summary)

records.source_title: The impact of bushfires on student wellbeing and student learning
records.mechanism: Risk is higher for students with limited family finances or support, family conflict or loss of social networks after the fire; schools restoring routine and hope help recovery
records.affected_group: children in low-resource or displaced families
records.quant_evidence: Most children recover; a substantial minority have persistent reactions

records.source_title: Women's experience of violence and intimate relationships after the Black Saturday bushfires (ANROWS-hosted report)
records.author_or_outlet: ANROWS (Australia's National Research Organisation for Women's Safety)
records.mechanism: Disaster strain (loss of control, stress, displacement, alcohol use) raises domestic and family violence in affected communities, some from previously non-violent partners
records.affected_group: women and children in affected communities
records.quant_evidence: Based on interviews with 47 service workers and 29 women

records.source_title: Impacts of the 2019-20 bushfires on the telecommunications network
records.mechanism: Mains power loss, not fire damage, caused most telecom outages, cutting communications for isolated holiday-area communities and businesses
records.affected_group: residents, businesses and tourists in fire areas
records.quant_evidence: 888 outages of 4+ hours (19 Dec-31 Jan); 88% from power outages, 1% direct fire damage; average 3.5 days; 1,406 facilities affected

records.source_title: Royal Commission into National Natural Disaster Arrangements, Report (via Energy Networks Australia summary of Recommendation 9)
records.author_or_outlet: Royal Commission into National Natural Disaster Arrangements / Energy Networks Australia
records.mechanism: Failure or loss of electricity networks disrupts communities and other critical infrastructure; the Commission asked networks and infrastructure operators to coordinate and harden vulnerable assets
records.quant_evidence: 80 recommendations in total

records.source_title: Bushfire disaster payment applications closing soon (Services Australia payment totals)
records.author_or_outlet: Australian Government (Minister for Agriculture / Services Australia figures)
records.mechanism: Flat payments to affected adults and children, plus income-replacement allowance for people who lost work, give quick cash to households but at a fixed rate that may not match actual loss
records.affected_group: affected adults, children, workers who lost income
records.quant_evidence: As of July 2020 over A$283m paid: A$233m disaster recovery payments (A$1,000 per adult, A$400 per child), A$15.9m disaster recovery allowance, A$34.7m child payments

records.source_title: Additional financial counselling services in bushfire affected areas
records.author_or_outlet: Department of Social Services (ministerial media release)
records.mechanism: Fire-affected households and businesses face disputes with insurers, trouble paying mortgage, rent and utility bills and debt negotiation, which governments address with extra financial counselling
records.affected_group: households and small businesses in financial hardship
records.quant_evidence: A$3.5m for additional financial counselling

records.source_title: South Coast, Snowies, Bega hit hardest financially from bushfires (reporting EY modelling for the National Bushfire Recovery Agency)
records.author_or_outlet: Canberra Times (reporting Ernst & Young for National Bushfire Recovery Agency)
records.place: NSW South Coast, Snowy Valleys; 96 LGAs nationally
records.mechanism: Fire hits tourism visitor numbers hardest (evacuation and summer downturn), producing direct and indirect (supply-chain) losses in small coastal and alpine economies
records.quant_evidence: A$3.6bn total hit across 96 LGAs; tourism A$1.9bn; Shoalhaven A$345m; Bega Valley A$218.9m (direct A$138.8m, indirect A$59.8m); visitors down 70-100% during January evacuations

records.source_title: South Coast, Snowies, Bega hit hardest financially from bushfires (EY modelling)
records.author_or_outlet: Canberra Times (reporting EY for National Bushfire Recovery Agency)
records.mechanism: Fire-burnt forests and herds cause multi-year declines in dairy output and forestry value (burnt timber sells at a fraction of price), cutting farm and timber income and local jobs
records.affected_group: dairy farmers, forestry workers and mills
records.quant_evidence: Agriculture A$1bn, forestry A$700m of losses; forestry assets lost 50-56% of value in Snowy Valleys; salvaged timber 10-20% of normal price; three years of declining dairy output

records.source_title: Final report of the 2009 Victorian Bushfires Royal Commission (underinsurance findings, via Insurance News)
records.author_or_outlet: 2009 Victorian Bushfires Royal Commission / Insurance News
records.mechanism: Sum-insured policies leave owners to estimate rebuild cost; without current building-cost information they underinsure, and uninsured or underinsured owners cannot rebuild fully
records.quant_evidence: About 30% of 2,029 destroyed homes underinsured; about 13% possibly uninsured; claims A$1.07bn vs A$4.4bn total cost

records.source_title: Lessons to be learned in relation to the Australian bushfire season 2019-20 (Senate Finance and Public Administration References Committee)
records.mechanism: Prolonged smoke cut trade and forced closures for retail and tourism businesses relying on summer holiday trade, but federal relief programs largely ignored smoke-only losses (smoke-affected businesses without direct fire damage got little help)
records.affected_group: smoke-affected small businesses (retail, tourism), e.g. ACT

records.source_title: Lessons to be learned in relation to the Australian bushfire season 2019-20 (Senate inquiry)
records.mechanism: Recovery is slow in regional areas and the inquiry focused on human health and welfare; stakeholders questioned coordination, equity and efficiency of recovery programs

records.source_title: Fire on the farm: assessing the impacts of the 2019-2020 bushfires on food and agriculture in Australia
records.author_or_outlet: WWF-Australia (NGO report; not a government source)
records.mechanism: Fire destroys farm buildings, fences, crops and livestock and lowers farmland value; insurance and grants cover only part of the loss
records.quant_evidence: A$2-3bn direct farm property damage; food production losses about A$2bn; over 100,000 livestock deaths; total A$4-5bn = 6-8% of agricultural output (secondary summary)

records.source_title: Fire on the farm (WWF) - grants share and farmer health
records.mechanism: Farmers and food businesses received a small share of recovery grants relative to their loss, and farmers suffered health effects, adding a health cost
records.quant_evidence: About 20% of government recovery grants went to farm/food businesses; farmer health impacts valued at A$279m (secondary summary)

records.source_title: The backbone of regional and rural economies: small business and community resilience
records.place: Townsville floods 2019 and Black Summer case studies
records.mechanism: Small businesses carry most of the economic impact in regional areas and are often under-insured, with weak business-interruption cover, so they struggle to restart and the local economy recovers slower
records.quant_evidence: Small business = 65-72% of total economic impact; Black Summer GDP impact about A$2.7bn; only 44% of flood-covered Townsville small businesses had business-interruption cover (ACCC survey, n=75)

records.source_title: NSW Bushfire Inquiry final report (summary by Mondaq)
records.author_or_outlet: Mondaq (law-firm summary of NSW Bushfire Inquiry 2020, Owens/O'Kane)
records.mechanism: Meeting bushfire building standards in fire zones is very expensive and many older dwellings do not meet them, so rebuilding or upgrading costs are a barrier and insurers want better risk data (BAL/APZ database) to price cover
records.quant_evidence: Compliance can add up to about A$100,000 to building cost

records.source_title: NSW Bushfire Inquiry final report (summary by Mondaq)
records.mechanism: Inquiry recommends subsidies for property owners to do mitigation works and working with insurers so that risk reduction lowers premiums (links mitigation spending to premium relief)
records.quant_evidence: 76 recommendations accepted by NSW Government

records.source_title: Volunteer compensation after bushfires (ACT)
records.mechanism: Volunteer firefighters lose paid work and business income while fighting fires; a federal compensation scheme exists but uptake was very low because many volunteers declined pay
records.affected_group: volunteer firefighters and their employers/own businesses
records.quant_evidence: Up to A$6,000 per volunteer at up to A$300/day; only 8 ACT volunteers applied, 6 paid

records.source_title: 'Fireballs bigger than a ute' torched Jamie's property. Five years later he's still living in a caravan
records.place: Bega Valley Shire, NSW South Coast
records.mechanism: Rebuilding is slow because new fire-safety building standards and slow development approvals raise cost and delay; many households stay in caravans, sheds or tents, so the destroyed-home count (DL) turns into long-run housing displacement (SL).
records.affected_group: Homeowners who lost houses, especially lower-income and older people
records.quant_evidence: About 50 of 464 destroyed homes rebuilt (~11%) five years on

records.source_title: 'Fireballs bigger than a ute' torched Jamie's property. Five years later he's still living in a caravan
records.place: Bega Valley Shire, NSW South Coast
records.mechanism: Fire-destroyed homes shrink rental supply while displaced households compete for the same rentals, pushing rents up and locking out low-income renters and older single women.
records.affected_group: Renters, displaced households, older single women
records.quant_evidence: Rents up over 30% in five years; single women over 50 described as fastest-growing homeless group nationally

records.source_title: 'Fireballs bigger than a ute' torched Jamie's property. Five years later he's still living in a caravan
records.place: Bega Valley Shire, NSW South Coast
records.mechanism: Government and charity money flows mainly to main-street and community projects, while housing recovery stalls on rules (transitional units judged non-compliant); public money is available but not reaching the housing gap, a who-gets-it problem.
records.affected_group: Residents without rebuilt homes; community groups
records.quant_evidence: $9.6m secured for main street rebuild; ~$800k community fund; $500k+ raised for transitional housing units

records.source_title: Black Summer bushfires anniversary: a struggling food industry one year on
records.place: NSW South Coast, Kangaroo Island SA
records.mechanism: Closure over the peak Christmas trading period plus fire bans wiped out a small cafe's annual income, leaving it unable to pay shopfront rent so it shut (lost turnover -> closure).
records.affected_group: Small hospitality business owners and staff

records.source_title: Black Summer bushfires anniversary: a struggling food industry one year on
records.place: Kangaroo Island SA; regional food producers
records.mechanism: Food producers lost restaurant and hotel supply contracts because the customers were closed, then COVID restrictions removed the recovery; online sales only partly offset it (supply-chain/customer loss).
records.affected_group: Small food producers and their casual staff

records.source_title: South Coast, Snowies, Bega hit hardest financially from bushfires
records.place: Shoalhaven, Bega Valley, Eurobodalla, Snowy Valleys NSW
records.mechanism: Modelled economic loss is concentrated in a few councils and dominated by tourism and hospitality, then agriculture and forestry (indirect loss follows industry mix).
records.quant_evidence: EY model: $3.6b total; tourism $1.9b; agriculture $1b; forestry $0.7b; 80% of loss in 30 LGAs; Shoalhaven $345m, Bega $218.9m

records.source_title: South Coast, Snowies, Bega hit hardest financially from bushfires
records.mechanism: Burnt timber can only be sold for a fraction of normal value and burned dairy/farm production falls for several seasons (stock and plantation loss -> multi-year farm income loss).
records.quant_evidence: Salvage timber 10-20% of normal price; three years of lower dairy output; 45% ag production fall projected in Snowy Valleys for a year

records.source_title: Councils cannot provide much more than 'moral support' after bushfires, royal commission told
records.mechanism: Councils say they have little capacity to absorb emergency response and recovery costs and depend on state/federal money; earlier fires (2016) got no assistance, so costs fall on local ratepayers (cost shifting / funding gap).

records.source_title: Councils cannot provide much more than 'moral support' after bushfires, royal commission told
records.place: NSW South Coast and Southern Tablelands
records.mechanism: Rising numbers of under- and uninsured owners, and some owners shut out of insurance by location, mean more of the loss is carried by households and, later, public budgets.

records.source_title: Batemans Bay rated the worst town in NSW for renters with pets
records.mechanism: Home loss combined with a large share of holiday-let and second homes leaves displaced locals competing for few long-term rentals; fire survivors search for many months and give up pets or risk homelessness.
records.quant_evidence: 27% of housing stock vacant year-round; 58% of rentals ban pets; one survivor searched 15 months; 500+ homes destroyed

records.source_title: Fire victims 'had to jump through hoops'
records.mechanism: Income-support rules assume steady income, so seasonal farm businesses struggle to prove eligibility; approval took weeks and agencies asked for conflicting paperwork (payment delay, administrative burden).
records.quant_evidence: 7 weeks to approve disaster recovery allowance; $250/week for 13 weeks; farm rebuild expected ~7 years

records.source_title: 'Community groups in the dark': Black Summer bushfire recovery grant announcements delayed
records.mechanism: Grant decisions slipped from December 2021 to February 2022 with no explanation, stalling small business and community projects (e.g. Eden temporary hospitality containers) two years after the fires (grant delay).
records.quant_evidence: ~$276m allocated over 2021-22 to 2023-24

records.source_title: Bureaucratic obstacles to recovery must go
records.mechanism: Road closures (Kings Highway), power outages spoiling stock, and a closed Eden timber mill meant lost holiday-period trade even in unburnt premises; one Mogo owner was wrongly refused Centrelink help (red tape).
records.quant_evidence: About 1,000 homes destroyed across the South Coast

records.source_title: South Coast businesses begin long road to recovery after summer inferno
records.mechanism: Even undamaged shops lost the peak summer trade as visitors stayed away, so owners cut casual staff hours and let workers go (turnover loss -> reduced hours/jobs, no physical damage needed).
records.affected_group: Casual hospitality and retail workers, small business owners
records.quant_evidence: A Narooma restaurant lost $160,000 trade in four weeks; Tilba shops cut staff from 4-6 to 1 per day

records.source_title: South Coast businesses begin long road to recovery after summer inferno
records.mechanism: Federal business grants required direct fire damage, so indirectly hit businesses (no customers) only qualified for low-interest loans, adding debt rather than cash (grant eligibility gap).

records.source_title: NSW bushfires' livestock death toll at more than 13,000 and rising
records.mechanism: Stock deaths and burnt pasture force farmers to rely on emergency fodder, water and volunteer fencing, which covers only the short run (livestock/pasture loss).
records.quant_evidence: 13,000+ head dead early; 10,500 t fodder distributed

records.source_title: Farmers could be left with the bill for replacing burned fences
records.mechanism: Law exempts Crown land (e.g. state forests) from sharing boundary fence cost, so neighbouring farmers face the replacement bill, a direct cost shift from the state to private owners.
records.quant_evidence: ~$10,000 per km of fence; govt subsidy up to $75,000 per farm

records.source_title: How climate change is contributing to soaring insurance costs
records.mechanism: As risk rises, insurers raise premiums or decline cover, so households in fire-prone areas face premium rises and some drop cover (premium rise and insurance withdrawal).
records.affected_group: Households and farmers in high-risk areas
records.quant_evidence: 1.8m households without home insurance; $15,000 annual premiums becoming normal in high-risk areas

records.source_title: Black Summer bushfires cost Australia billions in lost tourism, new research reveals
records.place: Australia, NSW most affected; Snowy Valleys
records.mechanism: Cancellations and negative coverage cut visitor spending across accommodation and aviation, producing lost output and jobs even in areas not burned (tourism flow loss).
records.affected_group: Tourism and hospitality workers and businesses
records.quant_evidence: $2.8b output and ~7,300 jobs lost nationally; NSW $1.1b; takings down over 70% in holiday period

records.source_title: Black Summer bushfires cost Australia billions in lost tourism, new research reveals
records.mechanism: Some mill workers left town early fearing job loss, and replacing them stayed hard years later (occupational mobility / labour-supply loss).
records.affected_group: Mill and manufacturing workers, local employers

records.source_title: Bushfire survivors still camping years later amid construction backlog
records.mechanism: A grant that encouraged new builds booked builders out for years, so households not yet ready fell back in the queue; builders and owner-builders are slowed by supply, permits and costs (construction bottleneck, benefits builders).
records.quant_evidence: $20,000 grant; 127 homes lost in and around Mallacoota; $600m+ recovery spend

records.source_title: Bushfire survivors still camping years later amid construction backlog
records.mechanism: Recovery support is fragmented and loses skilled caseworkers when funded recovery phases end, so help disappears before households are rehoused (service continuity).
records.quant_evidence: 25 caseworkers deployed initially

records.source_title: Conjola residents struggle to rebuild a year on from NSW bushfires as insurance battle rages
records.mechanism: Underinsurance and drawn-out disputes leave homeowners with payouts well below rebuild cost, so rebuilding stalls or is self-funded with new debt (underinsurance -> debt/delay).
records.quant_evidence: Some underinsured by about 50%; 89 houses lost, only a handful rebuilt after a year

records.source_title: Conjola residents struggle to rebuild a year on from NSW bushfires as insurance battle rages
records.mechanism: A flower farmer missed the planting season because the insurance claim was unsettled, delaying farm income by about two years (insurance delay -> lost production).
records.quant_evidence: About 2 years before income resumes

records.source_title: A crisis of underinsurance threatens to scar rural Australia permanently
records.mechanism: New building codes and post-disaster price spikes make rebuilding cost exceed sum insured; banks take part of payouts to clear mortgages; temporary housing cover is short, so owners take on larger mortgages or leave permanently (underinsurance/debt).
records.quant_evidence: >65% of Blue Mountains 2013 households underinsured; Vic survey 46% adequately insured; rebuild cost 20%+ above value; one case $550k cover ended in $700k mortgage

records.source_title: Mallacoota housing crisis deepens two years on from Black Summer fires
records.mechanism: With homes destroyed, essential workers (teachers, nursing and shop staff) leave because they cannot find or afford housing, which thins local services even as tourism returns (housing loss -> labour loss).
records.quant_evidence: Only 15 of 120 destroyed homes rebuilt; rent for modest 3BR $170 to $370/week

records.source_title: Mallacoota housing crisis deepens two years on from Black Summer fires
records.mechanism: Building materials surged in price after the fire and COVID, so some owners shrink or abandon rebuild plans (post-disaster construction inflation).
records.quant_evidence: Materials up ~30%; timber rise of 70% expected; 2-bed flat $250k to ~$450k

records.source_title: Black Summer bushfire survivors on NSW Far South Coast rebuild 12 months on from disaster
records.mechanism: Uninsured owners (premiums for a heritage building were too costly) depend on charity and donations to rebuild, and heritage approvals delay start of work (insurance gap, approval delay).
records.quant_evidence: 974 homes destroyed, 7 deaths on Far South Coast

records.source_title: The Black Summer bushfires were more than 6 months ago. How are affected communities coping?
records.mechanism: Big charities held back about half of donated money six months on while grassroots groups filled gaps; COVID removed mental health services from towns, delaying healing (funds disbursement lag, service withdrawal).
records.quant_evidence: $282m to three charities, just under half distributed by June

records.source_title: The Black Summer bushfires were more than 6 months ago. How are affected communities coping?
records.mechanism: Months of continuous work after disaster and prior drought left farmers exhausted, with one reporting suicidal thoughts before help arrived (mental health, farmer stress).

records.source_title: Farmers reflect on Black Summer fire recovery saying it's been tough, but not all bad
records.mechanism: Farm families take off-farm jobs to bridge the long gap before farm income returns, a switch in who earns the household income (income substitution / job mobility).
records.quant_evidence: Lost 13,300 of 14,000 plants; production recovery 4-5 years; a vegetable farm had employed 24 (4 full-time, 20 seasonal)

records.source_title: Farmers reflect on Black Summer fire recovery saying it's been tough, but not all bad
records.mechanism: A concessional recovery loan was refused after 12 months because the farm had no profit in the preceding drought years, so prior hardship excluded the household from help (grant/loan eligibility).
records.quant_evidence: 12-month application, rejected

records.source_title: New research shows Black Summer's megafires left lasting scars far beyond property damage
records.mechanism: Disrupted local business and tourism cut work hours and jobs, raising the share of households with zero or negative income (household income loss).
records.quant_evidence: +1.3 percentage points of households with no or negative income vs unburnt areas

records.source_title: New research shows Black Summer's megafires left lasting scars far beyond property damage
records.mechanism: Rents rise and displaced households double up with relatives, causing overcrowding; effects are larger in disadvantaged areas (rent and overcrowding).
records.quant_evidence: Rent +A$20/week (~10%); +A$26/week (13%) in disadvantaged areas

records.source_title: New research shows Black Summer's megafires left lasting scars far beyond property damage
records.mechanism: Recovery work adds long hours of unpaid labour, falling more on women (unpaid recovery work/gender).
records.quant_evidence: +1.7 pp women vs +1.0 pp men doing 15+ unpaid hours per week

records.source_title: As we begin to assess the fire damage in Victoria, we must not overlook these hidden costs
records.place: Victoria; draws on Black Summer evidence
records.mechanism: Flat government payments help a renter without savings far less than an insured owner with borrowing power, so recovery widens inequality (who benefits from aid).
records.quant_evidence: $1,000 payment example; rent rises $20-$26/week a year after Black Summer

records.source_title: How the bushfires affected our food producers
records.author_or_outlet: Good Fruit & Vegetables (Foden, Lindell, Brewer, Evans)
records.mechanism: Orchards lose trees and equipment and new plantings take years to pay back, hard on older growers already making little money (long-lag farm capital loss).
records.quant_evidence: 10-20% production loss; ~$110,000 of equipment lost on one farm; 7-10 year payback lag

records.source_title: How the bushfires affected our food producers
records.author_or_outlet: Good Fruit & Vegetables (Foden, Lindell, Brewer, Evans)
records.place: Canberra district and South Coast wine regions
records.mechanism: Cellar-door visits fell and smoke risked tainting ripening grapes, threatening both visitor income and the vintage (tourism plus smoke taint).
records.quant_evidence: Tourists about 40% of income for small-medium wineries

records.source_title: Farmers still finding their feet after Black Summer Bushfire
records.mechanism: Matched-dollar government replanting funds helped an orchardist rebuild, with recovery work taking about two years (public funds supporting farm recovery).
records.quant_evidence: ~25% of orchard lost; dollar-for-dollar replanting funding

records.source_title: Network Outages During Bushfire Season Lasted 3.5 Days On Average
records.mechanism: Power and mobile outages stopped payment terminals and bookings, so shops could not sell food or fuel and tourism lost booking access (infrastructure outage -> lost sales).
records.quant_evidence: 1,390 telecom facilities hit; average outage 3.5 days; 150 base stations and 20,000+ NBN services down at peak

records.source_title: BlazeAid rebuilding communities one fence at a time

records.source_title: Batlow Apples ripen after the flames, but full fire impact unknown

records.source_title: Last summer's bushfire season in top five disasters for insurance payouts

records.source_title: Rising insurance sees disaster victims call on politicians to address costs days out from election

records.source_title: Black Saturday rebuilding led to 'underutilised' infrastructure that pushed rates higher, residents say

records.source_title: Bushfire recovery chief highlights underinsurance burden

records.source_title: Students and staff move forward after the school holidays that never were
