sweep_notes.notes: About 45 records from about 35 distinct sources (some are institute reports, news summaries, or government documents, labelled in the author field as non-peer-reviewed, because few peer-reviewed items could be opened). Many publisher pages returned 403 (PreventionWeb, Stanford news, Monash, PubMed, UOW, Springer), so for those I relied on the figures shown in the search summary, not the full paper; treat Akter and Grafton, the arXiv labour-market paper, the Portugal paper, the Fort McMurray survey authorship, the Stanford smoke-test-score piece and the Marshall Fire study as needing a quick check of the original. Authors not confirmed for arXiv 2308.02739, the Portugal parish study and the Fort McMurray survey. Gaps: (1) opportunity cost of recovery spending has almost no direct empirical paper; the closest are Deryugina (hidden transfers), Liao and Kousky (budget deficit), and council submissions, so it is mostly an inference; (2) no peer-reviewed study found on insurance premium rises after a fire in Australia (only California news), so no record added; (3) Greece Mati and Portugal 2017 recovery economics: only damage figures in news, no peer-reviewed study found; (4) rent and displacement in Australia: only Akter and Grafton summary; (5) no Australian peer-reviewed paper found on workers who live elsewhere being laid off when a workplace burns (spillover), only supply-chain modelling (Reiner), Maui analogue and Groen et al.; (6) population loss and rate base in NSW not found; (7) no sources from ACM used. Scholar-style search could not open some paywalled PDFs; numbers marked 'not seen' were not verified."

Ran about 45 searches/fetches over 29 distinct documents (about 59 records). Many gov/agency PDFs came back as binary through WebFetch; I extracted text locally with pypdf for Deloitte (2 docs), Productivity Commission 2014 Vol 1, ANU/Phoenix survey summary, IDMC, TRA, Vic Parliament note, DRNSW evaluation. Others (RBA, ABS retail/labour, ACCC, AIHW, AIDR, NSW Education, ANROWS, Mandarin, Canberra Times, Region Canberra, insurancenews, REMPLAN) were read as web pages through the fetch summariser. Records built only from search-result summaries, not opened in full: Senate bushfire inquiry (aph.gov.au page returned 403), ACMA telecom review (infrastructure.gov.au fetch timed out; numbers from search summary), Services Australia payment totals, ICA total claims and A$2.32bn, IAG/SGS backbone report (403), NSW Education 600 school closures, WWF Fire on the Farm figures (preventionweb 403), ABS labour-force detail sentence about 5.1-5.3% unemployment. Treat those as needing a second check before citing. Gaps: the Royal Commission (2020) and NSW Bushfire Inquiry full PDFs were too large or timed out (10 MB fetch limit), so only thin records exist; no usable text from NSW Reconstruction Authority, IPART, Office of Local Government, Treasury or Productivity Commission post-2014 material; the Victorian 2009 Royal Commission is represented only via an insurance-trade-press summary. I found no government source giving quantified council revenue or rate-base loss after Black Summer (LGNSW rate relief pages 404). BNHCRC/Deakin Black Saturday income study and Akter/Grafton Black Summer household-income paper were identified in search but blocked (403/CAPTCHA), so not recorded; these are strong leads for IL/SL income mechanisms. No ACM sources used. The Mandarin, Canberra Times, Region Canberra, Reinsurance News, Mondaq, IAG/SGS and WWF items are secondary or non-government and are labelled as such."

Ran about 25 searches and about 55 page fetches (WebSearch + WebFetch only; no downloads). 63 records from 45 distinct articles/pages. Gaps: Guardian Australia and SMH are blocked from the search tool (domain filter rejected) so none are included; NPR returned 403; Blue Mountains Gazette fetched OK but SBS Blue Mountains piece is 2013. Local papers covered: Bega District News, Merimbula News Weekly, Milton Ulladulla Times, Blue Mountains Gazette, Border Mail, Daily Advertiser, The Land, Canberra Times, The Senior, Region/About Regional. No Tumut and Adelong Times, Lithgow Mercury, Port Macquarie News, Northern Rivers papers pages were read. Hard to find: first-person accounts with numbers on DV (no NSW 2019-20 statistics found; DV mechanism rests on Black Saturday research cited by news), real council budget/rate-rise numbers after Black Summer (only the Eurobodalla rate-reimbursement shortfall, taken from a search summary of the council page, and the 2009 Marysville case), opportunity-cost-of-recovery-spending evidence (best proxies: NSW treasurer quote and Marysville infrastructure case), and insurance premium rise numbers after Black Summer specifically. Caveats: fetched summaries came through a small model, so numbers should be spot-checked before citing; the Per Capita/GetUp spending report is advocacy-commissioned; the Conversation 2025 piece summarises other researchers' work. Items from non-NSW (Vic) and non-Black Summer events (Black Saturday 2009, Blue Mountains 2013, Pomonal 2024, Vic 2026) are labelled in the disaster field. Mortgage-stress, debt and savings-drawdown, and DV records are thin on direct numbers; worth targeting in peer-reviewed or survey sweeps.

About 25 searches and 40 page fetches. 63 records from about 38 distinct sources or studies (a few are Black Saturday 2009 or Maui 2023 comparisons, flagged by disaster field). Many pages returned 403 (unimelb Pursuit, PreventionWeb Akter and Grafton original, Scimex, Eurobodalla Business Confidence PDFs), so a few records rest on search-result summaries (ALGA 62 million, Vinnies, Akter and Grafton, FHTA, medRxiv, Climate Council, The New Daily) and are marked as such; no numbers were invented. Year and authors of the Akter and Grafton study were not visible (marked n/d). Several PDFs (Asthma Australia smoke survey, NSW Farmers survey results, Business NSW tourism survey, ANU PDF detail, Hazard Note financial detail) did not give readable text. Non-survey items (EY, WWF/Sydney, Reiner input-output, census difference-in-differences, Auditor-General) are labelled as modelling or administrative data; they are included because they carry the numbers, but source-type counts should treat them as secondary. Not found or not fetched: Red Cross Black Summer report, Tourism Research Australia survey, Mission Australia, HILDA Black Summer-specific results, Australian Unity Index numbers, Business NSW survey, council interview studies on cost shifting and opportunity cost of recovery spending (no direct source found; Auditor-General BLER and ALGA records are the closest), and any survey on population loss or rate base. Gaps: little quantitative evidence for job-switching costs, savings drawdown, power/telecom/road outage, and opportunity cost of recovery spending. The 46% turnover drop in a 177-business Bega survey appeared in a search summary but I could not tie it to a specific URL, so it is omitted. No ACM sources used. Nothing downloaded except PDF text read from tool cache."

mechanisms.name: Homes and buildings destroyed (direct loss base, partly insured)
mechanisms.description: Fire destroys homes, facilities and outbuildings -> direct physical loss; insurers pay part of it, so insured claims are only a fraction of the true loss and the rest falls on households and governments
mechanisms.pillar_note: DL: homes/facilities destroyed per council; insured claims value as a cross-check
mechanisms.key_quant_evidence: NSW: 2,448 homes and 284 facilities destroyed, A$1.88bn insurance cost (AIDR); later ICA totals 38,181 claims, A$2.32bn (Reinsurance News); insured losses about A$2.2bn (MJA-Lancet)

mechanisms.name: Farm capital destroyed (livestock, fencing, pasture, orchards, equipment)
mechanisms.description: Fire kills stock and burns fences, pasture, trees and machinery -> farm capital and land value fall; farmers must buy fodder and rebuild before earning again, and drought makes it worse
mechanisms.pillar_note: DL: livestock deaths, fencing km and farm assets lost per council (strengthens the farm part of DL)
mechanisms.key_quant_evidence: Over 56,000 livestock killed or euthanised, median 20% of stock on affected farms (Cowled et al. AVJ); A$4-5bn farm losses, 6-8% of ag output (WWF/USyd); 6,284 head lost in NSW, 5,198 in South-East NSW (NSW DPI via Farmer Magazine)

mechanisms.name: Multi-year lag in farm income (replanting, herd rebuild, delayed claims)
mechanisms.description: Burnt orchards, herds and crops take years to come back, and slow insurance claims mean missed planting seasons -> farm income stays low for several years; families take off-farm jobs to fill the gap
mechanisms.pillar_note: IL: farm income / agricultural output in fire-hit councils, 1-5 years after
mechanisms.key_quant_evidence: Dairy output down for 3 years, Snowy Valleys ag production -45% projected for a year (EY via Canberra Times); orchard payback 7-10 years (Good Fruit & Vegetables)

mechanisms.name: Forestry supply shock -> mill jobs lost
mechanisms.description: Plantations and native forest burn -> burnt logs sell for a fraction of value and sawlog supply drops for decades -> mills close or cut staff; a few salvage mills hire temporarily
mechanisms.pillar_note: IL: jobs in wood/timber manufacturing workplaces in forestry councils (Snowy Valleys, Bega Valley)
mechanisms.affected_group: Timber workers, mills, Snowy Valleys economy
mechanisms.key_quant_evidence: Forestry A$700m loss, salvage timber 10-20% of normal price (EY via Canberra Times); about 5,000 jobs linked to timber, Hyne mill 230 workers (Border Mail)

mechanisms.name: Smoke taint on grapes and wine
mechanisms.description: Smoke taints grapes -> crops rejected or wine unsaleable, plus fewer cellar-door visitors -> winery income falls even without flames
mechanisms.pillar_note: IL: farm income in wine regions; smoke days as the exposure (not burned area)
mechanisms.key_quant_evidence: Industry estimate about A$40m, NSW association up to A$100m incl. tourism (ABC/MDPI); tourists about 40% of income for small wineries (Good Fruit & Vegetables)

mechanisms.name: Peak-season tourism shutdown in fire regions
mechanisms.description: Fires and evacuation orders over Christmas-January -> visitors cancel or are ordered out -> tourism and hospitality turnover collapses in the fire region; peak-season income is not made up later, partial rebound when visitors return
mechanisms.pillar_note: IL: regional visitor spend / accommodation takings by quarter; tourism jobs at workplaces in fire councils
mechanisms.affected_group: Regional tourism and hospitality businesses and workers
mechanisms.key_quant_evidence: South Coast NSW visitor spend -23% (A$251m) in Mar qtr 2020 (TRA); Bega Valley/Eurobodalla lost 70-100% of tourists for two weeks in January (EY); about half of 120 Merimbula chamber members had takings down 60%+

mechanisms.name: Tourism and supply-chain spillover to unburned places
mechanisms.description: Lost visitor spending flows back through suppliers, and travellers avoid whole regions -> jobs and output fall in unburned towns, other sectors and other states; some unaffected regions gain displaced spending
mechanisms.pillar_note: IL: indirect loss in neighbouring/unburned councils (spillover term); warns that burned area alone understates IL
mechanisms.affected_group: Supplier industries, accommodation in non-burnt towns
mechanisms.key_quant_evidence: A$2.8b total output loss vs A$1.7b direct (61% spillover), ~7,300 jobs nationally, 3,171 NSW (Reiner et al. 2024, input-output model); non-affected Vic towns 10-60% cancellations (FHTA); up to 28% of Maui loss outside Maui (UHERO)

mechanisms.name: Turnover loss in undamaged businesses -> fewer hours for casual staff
mechanisms.description: Fewer customers, travel disruption and supplier problems -> undamaged shops and food producers lose cash flow -> owners cut casual hours and let staff go
mechanisms.pillar_note: IL: business turnover / hours worked in fire councils, including businesses with no physical damage
mechanisms.affected_group: Small business owners, casual retail and hospitality workers
mechanisms.key_quant_evidence: Retail -0.3% in Jan 2020, department stores -2.2%, ACT -2.3% (ABS); two-thirds of 500 SMEs affected, mostly indirectly (NAB survey); a Narooma restaurant lost A$160,000 in four weeks (Bega District News)

mechanisms.name: Small business closure (cash-flow failure, anchor facility lost)
mechanisms.description: Lost peak trade plus thin cash buffers and weak business-interruption cover -> small firms close or depend on aid; loss of an anchor facility takes seasonal jobs from nearby towns
mechanisms.pillar_note: IL: business counts / closures (ABS CABEE) in fire councils
mechanisms.affected_group: Small and young businesses and their staff
mechanisms.key_quant_evidence: 17% of SMEs closed temporarily, 24% in vulnerable areas (NAB); small business 65-72% of economic impact, only 44% had BI cover in Townsville (IAG/SGS); Selwyn resort shut 3+ years, ~100 seasonal jobs (ABC)

mechanisms.name: Power, telecom and road outages stop trade
mechanisms.description: Mains power loss (not fire damage) knocks out phone towers, EFTPOS and bookings, and roads close -> towns cannot trade or sell fuel and food for days; stock spoils
mechanisms.pillar_note: IL: outage-days per council as a short-run IL driver; X: dependence on single power/road link
mechanisms.affected_group: Businesses and residents in cut-off towns
mechanisms.key_quant_evidence: 888 outages of 4+ hours, 88% from power loss and 1% from fire damage, average 3.5 days, 1,406 facilities (ACMA); 818 Telstra facilities hit in NSW

mechanisms.name: Smoke -> missed work and lower productivity far from fires
mechanisms.description: Smoke makes workers sick or stay home -> hours and earnings fall even in cities with no fire, a productivity loss
mechanisms.pillar_note: IL: smoke-day exposure as an IL driver separate from burned area
mechanisms.key_quant_evidence: Each extra smoke day lowers quarterly earnings ~0.1% (Borgschulte et al., US); 1.8 million Australians missed work, A$1.3bn+ output (Australia Institute poll); Sydney smoke A$12-50m/day (Climate Council)

mechanisms.name: Local employment and earnings fall, concentrated in land- and visitor-based sectors
mechanisms.description: Workplace damage and lost demand -> employment and wage income fall in fire areas, hardest in agriculture, retail and tourism, for up to a few years
mechanisms.pillar_note: IL: jobs and wage income at workplaces inside or near the fire outline, by industry
mechanisms.key_quant_evidence: Black Saturday: ~10% income loss vs matched areas; agriculture -31%, retail -13%, tourism -12% (Ulubasoglu & Beaini, AJEM); Maui unemployment 2.3% to 14.2% (UHERO)

mechanisms.name: Evacuation keeps workers away from jobs
mechanisms.description: Evacuation and road closures keep people from work; the longer they are away, the more work and income are lost, and some do not return to work for months
mechanisms.pillar_note: IL: work days lost to evacuation (evacuation orders x population) as a short-run IL term
mechanisms.key_quant_evidence: 55% of those away more than a night said it reduced their ability to work vs 37% (IDMC); about 1 in 4 Fort McMurray evacuated workers not back in paid work at follow-up (CMAJ Open)

mechanisms.name: Rebuilding and health sectors gain (sectoral winners)
mechanisms.description: Rebuilding spending, insurance payouts and health demand -> construction, real-estate and health workers earn more, partly offsetting losses; this can hide losses in aggregate GRP
mechanisms.pillar_note: IL: net vs gross indirect loss; construction jobs as an offset term in IL
mechanisms.key_quant_evidence: Healthcare workers +8% income (Ulubasoglu & Beaini); after Qld floods low earners -A$3,100, middle/high +A$3,770/+A$3,380 (Ulubasoglu 2020); US hurricane earnings negative year 1, positive from year 3 (Groen et al.)

mechanisms.name: Housing loss drives workers out -> local labour shortage
mechanisms.description: Destroyed homes and rising rents -> teachers, nurses, shop and mill staff leave -> employers cannot fill jobs and local services thin even as demand returns
mechanisms.pillar_note: IL: labour supply / job vacancies in fire towns; links SL housing to IL
mechanisms.affected_group: Essential and service workers, local employers
mechanisms.key_quant_evidence: Mallacoota: only 15 of 120 destroyed homes rebuilt, modest 3BR rent A$170 to A$370/week (ABC)

mechanisms.name: Moving away after the fire costs income
mechanisms.description: Households that relocate lose local networks and well-matched jobs -> larger income loss than those who stay; overseas evidence says the effect may fade within a few years
mechanisms.pillar_note: SL: household income of movers vs stayers; population change in fire councils
mechanisms.key_quant_evidence: Relocators about -19% income (Ulubasoglu & Beaini); Katrina displaced: small, mostly temporary income effects (Deryugina et al.)

mechanisms.name: Household income falls in severely burned communities
mechanisms.description: Disrupted local business and tourism cut hours and jobs -> weekly personal income falls and more households have zero or negative income, most in highest-severity areas
mechanisms.pillar_note: SL: median household/personal income change (Census 2016-2021 at SA1/SA2) by burn severity
mechanisms.key_quant_evidence: +1.3 percentage points of households with no or negative income vs unburnt (Akter & Grafton, The Conversation); nearly 20% of Lahaina respondents had income fall by more than half (UHERO via Civil Beat)

mechanisms.name: Financial hardship, debt stress and poverty
mechanisms.description: Lost income plus uninsured costs -> trouble paying mortgage, rent and bills, delinquency and bankruptcy for credit-constrained households; insured owners may instead pay down debt
mechanisms.pillar_note: SL: financial hardship / poverty share; could use mortgage arrears or hardship-payment counts
mechanisms.key_quant_evidence: Harvey: ~20% rise in bankruptcies, 13% rise in severe delinquency for uninsured credit-constrained owners (Billings et al.); Maui poverty 14% to 29% (UHERO); A$3.5m extra financial counselling (DSS)

mechanisms.name: Housing stock loss -> rents up and overcrowding
mechanisms.description: Destroyed homes shrink supply while displaced households compete for rentals (plus holiday-let share) -> rents rise, overcrowding and homelessness risk grow, worst for low-income renters
mechanisms.pillar_note: SL: median rent change and rental affordability (bond lodgements by postcode); overcrowding
mechanisms.key_quant_evidence: Rent +A$20/week (~10%), +A$26 (13%) in disadvantaged areas after Black Summer (Akter & Grafton); Camp Fire: nearby prices +13% within six weeks (Hennighausen & James); Bega Valley: 1 of 16 rentals affordable for a minimum-wage family (Anglicare)

mechanisms.name: Slow rebuilding -> long-term displacement
mechanisms.description: Bushfire building standards, approvals, material inflation and builder shortages raise cost and delay rebuilds -> families live in caravans, sheds or pods for years; case support ends before they are rehoused
mechanisms.pillar_note: SL: share of destroyed homes rebuilt after N years (building approvals / completions in fire areas)
mechanisms.affected_group: Homeowners who lost houses, older and lower-income people
mechanisms.key_quant_evidence: Bega Valley: ~50 of 464 destroyed homes rebuilt after five years (SBS); BAL compliance can add up to ~A$100,000 (NSW Inquiry via Mondaq); rebuilds can take 3-4 years (IDMC)

mechanisms.name: Underinsurance turns loss into household debt and stalled rebuilds
mechanisms.description: Low sums insured, debris costs inside the sum insured and rising rebuild costs -> payouts fall short -> owners take bigger mortgages, rely on charity, or never rebuild
mechanisms.pillar_note: Moderates DL -> SL: share underinsured/uninsured changes how much DL becomes household loss; also feeds FP when governments fill the gap
mechanisms.affected_group: Homeowners and small businesses in fire-prone areas
mechanisms.key_quant_evidence: Black Saturday: ~30% of 2,029 destroyed homes underinsured, ~13% possibly uninsured (Royal Commission); >65% of Blue Mountains 2013 households underinsured (ABC); Marshall Fire 74% underinsured (CU Boulder)

mechanisms.name: Premiums and insurance taxes push people out of cover
mechanisms.description: Address-level risk pricing, levies and stamp duty raise premiums -> households cut or drop cover before a fire; after a fire, perceived risk pushes premiums up further; mitigation could lower them
mechanisms.pillar_note: X / Moderator: pre-fire insurance affordability (premium-to-income) as an exposure condition; post-fire premium rise as an SL cost
mechanisms.affected_group: Households and small businesses in high-risk areas
mechanisms.key_quant_evidence: Emergency Services Levy and taxes over 50% of NSW premiums (ICA via Insurance News); 1.8m households without home insurance (Canberra Times); monthly-payment surcharges up to 20% (ACCC)

mechanisms.name: Fire exposure -> long-lasting mental ill-health
mechanisms.description: Life threat, loss and evacuation -> PTSD, depression and anxiety that stay high for years, reducing capacity to work and adding health costs
mechanisms.pillar_note: SL: mental-health service use (MBS mental-health items, GP visits) per 1,000 in fire areas
mechanisms.affected_group: Directly exposed adults and young people
mechanisms.key_quant_evidence: About 1 in 5 high-exposure people at PTSD cut-off 12-18 months on, n=3,083 (ANU survey); PTSD 21% at 5 years in high-impact Black Saturday communities (Beyond Bushfires); ~62.6% felt recovered at 10 years

mechanisms.name: Financial loss itself causes distress (incl. people outside burnt areas)
mechanisms.description: Lost income and later money troubles -> distress and worse mental health, even for people far from the fire front; second-wave stressors predict poor recovery
mechanisms.pillar_note: SL: links IL to SL; distress among indirectly affected people outside fire postcodes
mechanisms.key_quant_evidence: Almost three-quarters of indirectly affected respondents had anxiety symptoms up to two years on (ANU); over half of Black Saturday survivors had extra stressful events such as financial difficulty (Beyond Bushfires)

mechanisms.name: Lower life satisfaction (wellbeing cost)
mechanisms.description: Disaster -> life satisfaction lower for 18+ months; valued in dollars this is a large cost not in damage tallies
mechanisms.pillar_note: SL: wellbeing score (HILDA life satisfaction) as an SL indicator
mechanisms.key_quant_evidence: Significantly lower life satisfaction after 18 months (HILDA, Life Course Centre); willingness to pay ~A$2,991 per household per year for 1% less impact (Ambrey et al.)

mechanisms.name: Responder trauma
mechanisms.description: Long deployments and life-threat exposure -> PTSD and distress among firefighters and emergency staff, affecting later work and volunteering
mechanisms.pillar_note: SL: health of responders; X: volunteer brigade density
mechanisms.affected_group: Fire and emergency volunteers and employees
mechanisms.key_quant_evidence: 4,000+ personnel; 31% of volunteers felt life at risk; probable PTSD/distress 4.2% volunteers, 7.3% employees two years on (Curtin After the Fires)

mechanisms.name: Volunteer firefighting and recovery work costs lost income
mechanisms.description: Volunteers spend weeks away from paid work or their own business -> lost income for them and their employers; compensation exists but uptake is low; volunteer recovery (fencing) shifts cost from budgets to charity time
mechanisms.pillar_note: SL/IL: volunteer days away from paid work per council; FP: compensation payments
mechanisms.affected_group: Volunteer firefighters, small employers, farmers helped
mechanisms.key_quant_evidence: 1.84 million volunteer days, A$143.5m paid leave, A$116.5m unpaid leave (Curtin final report); ~64,500 of 82,480 responders were volunteers (WSU); only 8 ACT volunteers applied for compensation

mechanisms.name: Unpaid recovery work falls on women
mechanisms.description: Clean-up, caring and household recovery work increase -> more unpaid hours, mostly women, less time for paid work
mechanisms.pillar_note: SL: Census unpaid domestic work hours by sex
mechanisms.key_quant_evidence: +1.7 pp women vs +1.0 pp men doing 15+ unpaid hours/week in burnt areas (Akter & Grafton)

mechanisms.name: Domestic and family violence rises
mechanisms.description: Stress, financial and housing loss, alcohol, and stretched or cut-off services -> more domestic violence, including from previously non-violent partners; evacuation centres expose women to former partners
mechanisms.pillar_note: SL: DV incidents per 1,000 (BOCSAR, monthly by LGA)
mechanisms.key_quant_evidence: Women in worst-affected Black Saturday areas reported IPV ~7 times the rate of less-affected (Flinders review); 16 of 30 women reported violence since the fires, 9 new (Parkinson, AJEM)

mechanisms.name: School closures and displacement disrupt schooling
mechanisms.description: Fires close schools, damage facilities, take teachers away and displace children -> lost school days and more counselling and food support needs
mechanisms.pillar_note: SL: school closure days / attendance in fire councils
mechanisms.key_quant_evidence: About 600 NSW schools closed in late 2019 (CESE media summary); 14,500 children among ~65,000 displaced (Central Western Daily); 403 of 687 Milton PS pupils directly affected

mechanisms.name: Delayed learning and child wellbeing harm
mechanisms.description: Trauma, family stress, temporary housing and smoke -> children's behaviour and test-score gains fall, with the lag showing years later
mechanisms.pillar_note: SL: NAPLAN gain in high-impact schools; child wellbeing
mechanisms.key_quant_evidence: 24,642 students: reading and numeracy gains reduced at 2 and 4 years in high-impact schools (Gibbs et al.); smoke effect on test scores nearly doubles with heavy smoke days (Stanford, ~11,700 US districts)

mechanisms.name: Smoke health burden and health-system cost
mechanisms.description: Smoke -> deaths, hospital admissions, ED visits and symptoms well beyond burnt areas -> health-system and household costs
mechanisms.pillar_note: SL: respiratory ED visits/admissions per 1,000; FP: public health spending
mechanisms.affected_group: People with heart/lung conditions, smoke-affected cities
mechanisms.key_quant_evidence: 417 excess deaths, 3,151 hospitalisations, ~A$1.95b health cost, NSW A$1.07b (Borchers Arriagada et al., MJA); NSW respiratory ED visits up to 50% higher in some areas (AIHW)

mechanisms.name: Pre-existing disadvantage amplifies loss
mechanisms.description: Low earners, women, renters and Aboriginal people have smaller buffers -> lose more income and wellbeing, so fires widen inequality; fire-exposed places are often already older and poorer
mechanisms.pillar_note: Moderator on SL/IL: pre-fire SEIFA, renter share, Indigenous share as interaction terms with exposure
mechanisms.affected_group: Low-income people, women, renters, Aboriginal people
mechanisms.key_quant_evidence: Black Saturday: low-income -18%, women -14% vs men -9%, renters -14% (Ulubasoglu & Beaini); agricultural workers lost ~A$8,000/yr for two years (Ulubasoglu 2020)

mechanisms.name: Social ties protect recovery
mechanisms.description: Strong community and group membership -> better recovery and resilience (though close ties also mean more personal loss)
mechanisms.pillar_note: Moderator on SL: volunteering / community group rates as a protective X variable
mechanisms.key_quant_evidence: Almost 80% reported some resilience; about two-thirds return to pre-disaster wellbeing (ANU survey)

mechanisms.name: Public payments and charity cushion the loss
mechanisms.description: Flat disaster payments, income allowances, back-to-school grants, replanting funds and charity cash -> fast relief that offsets part of income loss, but at fixed rates not matched to need
mechanisms.pillar_note: Moderator on SL; also FP spending: disaster payments per capita by LGA
mechanisms.key_quant_evidence: Over A$283m paid by July 2020 (A$1,000/adult, A$400/child) (Services Australia); Red Cross over A$119m to 4,380 people (IDMC); 200,000+ individual payments (SBS)

mechanisms.name: Grant eligibility gaps exclude indirectly hit businesses and households
mechanisms.description: Grants require physical damage, steady income or prior profit, with sharp income thresholds -> smoke- or trade-hit firms and drought-hit farms get loans or nothing, adding debt rather than cash
mechanisms.pillar_note: Moderator on IL/SL (grant access); FP: share of loss eligible for support
mechanisms.key_quant_evidence: Only 7 of 90 Merimbula respondents had physical damage, so most were ineligible (Region); ~60% of SMEs wanted cash grants (NAB); one Cobargo applicant missed a threshold by A$27

mechanisms.name: Recovery grants slow, opaque and politically allocated
mechanisms.description: Reimbursement-style grants, delays and minimum thresholds set by ministers -> money arrives late and goes to some electorates over others; charities also hold back funds
mechanisms.pillar_note: FP: grant timing and allocation by council (BLER/BCRRF per capita vs DL)
mechanisms.key_quant_evidence: BLER A$541.8m with A$1m minimum threshold (Audit Office NSW); 26 first-round grants to Coalition seats, 0 to Blue Mountains (Inside Local Government); ~48% of A$2.74b delivered by end 2020 (SBS)

mechanisms.name: Who benefits from aid (targeting and regressivity)
mechanisms.description: Recovery money goes mainly to business, infrastructure and main-street projects, and to people with assets and borrowing power -> households, renters and farmers get less, so aid can widen gaps
mechanisms.pillar_note: FP: share of recovery spending reaching households vs businesses vs infrastructure
mechanisms.key_quant_evidence: Qld floods: ~10% of recovery spending to income help, ~80% to businesses (Ulubasoglu); ~20% of recovery grants to farm/food businesses (WWF); Harvey SBA/FEMA aid regressive (Billings et al.)

mechanisms.name: Who pays / opportunity cost of recovery spending
mechanisms.description: Large recovery budgets (shared Commonwealth/NSW) -> money spent rebuilding is not spent on mitigation or other services; facilities rebuilt for a shrunken town later force rate rises
mechanisms.pillar_note: FP: recovery spend per capita vs mitigation spend; council maintenance burden of rebuilt assets
mechanisms.key_quant_evidence: Commonwealth mitigation spend ~3% of post-disaster spend (Productivity Commission 2014); A$4.4bn NSW recovery programs, NSW share A$3bn (Regional NSW); Marysville A$1.72m/yr maintenance, 18% rate rise proposed (ABC)

mechanisms.name: Council budget gap (lost revenue plus extra spending)
mechanisms.description: Fires raise council spending and cut rates and fee income (rate relief only partly reimbursed) -> net deficit and crowd-out of roads and services, worst for small rural councils
mechanisms.pillar_note: FP: council own-source revenue gap and operating result (NSW OLG data) after fires
mechanisms.key_quant_evidence: California: deficit probability +25 pp, excess revenue -US$97/person (Liao & Kousky); Lockyer Valley A$42.5m = 88% of annual revenue (PC submission); Eurobodalla rate reimbursement ~A$300,000 short

mechanisms.name: Cost shifting between governments and onto private owners
mechanisms.description: Reimbursement rules shift costs up to the Commonwealth (weak mitigation incentive) and down to councils/ratepayers for unfunded items; Crown land exemption shifts fence costs to farmers
mechanisms.pillar_note: FP: unfunded share of council recovery costs (DRFA claims vs council spend)
mechanisms.affected_group: Councils, farmers next to state forest, taxpayers
mechanisms.key_quant_evidence: Commonwealth paid up to 75% above thresholds (Productivity Commission); fence ~A$10,000/km, subsidy up to A$75,000/farm (Border Mail)

mechanisms.name: Hidden fiscal cost through ordinary transfers and flow-on costs
mechanisms.description: Beyond visible disaster aid, governments pay more in unemployment, health and welfare transfers for years plus clean-up and temporary housing -> true fiscal cost is a multiple of reported aid
mechanisms.pillar_note: FP: welfare/JobSeeker recipients per LGA after fire as a hidden-cost indicator
mechanisms.key_quant_evidence: US hurricanes: fiscal cost per person ~US$150 rises to at least US$780 with transfers (Deryugina); Australia disasters A$38bn/yr average (Deloitte)

mechanisms.name: Property values and the rate base
mechanisms.description: Buyers re-price fire risk (values dip near fire zones) but housing shortage can push rebuilt-town prices up -> changes household wealth and the council rate base
mechanisms.pillar_note: FP: rateable land values (NSW Valuer General) in fire councils; SL: household wealth
mechanisms.key_quant_evidence: California 2018-21: homes farther from past fires ~2% higher value (FRBSF); Kinglake prices ~+150% in 10 years (agent comment); Mallacoota listings 84 to 20

mechanisms.name: Compounding disasters slow recovery
mechanisms.description: Fires followed by COVID, floods and mice -> relief centres close, bookings stay weak and capacity to recover erodes
mechanisms.pillar_note: Moderator / X: number of declared disasters in prior and following years per LGA
mechanisms.key_quant_evidence: Eurobodalla agency occupancy ~50% weekday, ~70% weekend to mid-December 2022 (About Regional)

mechanisms.name: Tourism dependence and peak-season timing set exposure
mechanisms.description: Councils with big tourism, agriculture or forestry shares, hit during the Christmas peak, lose much more for the same fire
mechanisms.pillar_note: X: tourism/ag/forestry employment share and fire month as exposure variables in the RF
mechanisms.key_quant_evidence: EY: 80% of A$3.6b loss in 30 LGAs, tourism A$1.9b (Canberra Times); 202 interviews and 1,004 survey responses on Christmas-period displacement (BNHCRC Hazard Note 95)

normalise.notes:
253 records were merged into 45 mechanisms (DL 2, IL 13, FP 7, SL 13, X 1, Moderator 9). 249 records are assigned and 4 are dropped. The dropped ones are about method or data gaps, not causal chains. gov-3, gov-5 and gov-9 are Deloitte and Productivity Commission notes on what is measured and how flow-on costs are modelled. gov-19 says ABS could not collect survey data in fire regions in Jan-Feb 2020, which matters as a data warning for IL tests. To get frequency by source type, count the record_id prefixes: lit = peer-reviewed literature, gov = government/inquiry, news = news/first-person, survey = survey/interview.

Duplicates to watch when counting:
- The same URL sits behind several records: Reiner et al. tourism (lit-1, lit-2, survey-23); EY via Canberra Times (gov-53, gov-54, news-6, news-7, survey-18, survey-19); Ulubasoglu and Beaini (lit-6 to lit-10, survey-34 to survey-37); Akter and Grafton (lit-3 to lit-5, survey-30 to survey-32, news-33 to news-35); the Insurance News Nixon speech (news-58, survey-6, survey-7).
- The independent-source count is therefore lower than the raw record count for M06, M07, M12, M17, M19 and M21. Unique URLs per mechanism are a better frequency measure.

Who pays / opportunity cost of recovery spending is M39 (FP) and has direct support (Productivity Commission, NSW Regional evaluation, the Treasurer via Canberra Times, ACT Treasury, ABC Marysville). Related FP chains are split out as M37 (grant process and politics), M38 (aid targeting), M40 (council budget gap), M41 (cost shifting) and M42 (hidden transfers).

Several key numbers are not Australian or come from a model, so they should not be treated as NSW observed effects:
- US analogues: Liao & Kousky, Deryugina, Borgschulte, Billings.
- Maui (UHERO).
- Input-output and EY estimates are modelled, not observed.

Evidence is thin in a few places:
- The M43 Kinglake figure is an agent's comment.
- lit-45 (A$52,300 psychological cost) was not method-checked.
- news-43 (Eurobodalla shortfall) came from a search summary.
- survey-2 (indirectly affected anxiety) was not checked in the PDF.

Pillar choices that could go either way:
- M10 outages: put in IL, though the underlying damage is DL.
- M27 volunteer lost income: SL, could be IL.
- M43 property values: FP rate base, could be SL wealth.
- M22 premiums: Moderator, could be X.

mappings.exp7_result: Homes destroyed per 1,000 dwellings tracks fire size (rank +0.65, Day 1). Pre-fire map predicts which councils lose homes (AUC 0.91 for Black Summer); how many homes per fire only partly predictable (Day 2). Council scale only; SA2 homes-inside-fire dose built in Day 9. Insured claims value was only quoted from the literature, not tested.

test_ideas.title: Does tourism and farm dependence make the same fire cost more? (exposure interaction on SA2 Black Summer panel)
test_ideas.indicator_strengthened: X variable (tourism/agriculture employment share, pre-fire disadvantage) as moderator of IL and SL; also sharpens the farm part of DL
test_ideas.data: Census 2016 industry share (accommodation and food, agriculture) and SEIFA 2016 by SA2; Experiment 7's SA2 total income (ABS PIA) and CABEE business counts panel; fire footprint x fire start month already in project
test_ideas.fire_matching: Use the Day 9 dose (share of an SA2's homes inside the fire outline, 57-72 treated SA2s). Split treated SA2s into high vs low tourism share (top tercile vs bottom) and by whether the fire reached them in Nov-Jan peak vs other months. Event time: fire year, year 1, year 2, as in Day 9, with the same SA2 and Sydney/rest-of-NSW year effects and future-fire placebo.
test_ideas.gap_filling: Census-year shares are used as fixed pre-fire weights, so no filling. Peak-season timing uses the fire's reported start date; where an SA2 was hit by several fires, take the earliest date with more than 10% homes inside outline (a stated rule, like the homes-inside-fire estimate).
test_ideas.expected_direction: Total income fall (-1.6% per 10 pp at year 2 on average) larger in high tourism or farming SA2s and in Christmas-peak fires; interaction effect expected negative but probably small and imprecise with about 60 treated SA2s, so report as an upper bound if not detected.
test_ideas.files_and_sizes: Census 2016 GCP DataPacks for NSW SA2 (about 5-16 MB, ABS DataPacks page); SEIFA 2016 SA2 xlsx (about 1-2 MB, ABS SEIFA page); no new fire data. ABS PIA and CABEE are already in Experiment 7.
test_ideas.risks: Only about 60 treated SA2s, essentially one season; tourism share is correlated with coastal location and with COVID border effects in 2020-21; Census 2016 industry is by residence, not workplace (use POWP via TableBuilder to improve).

test_ideas.title: Farm loss in South-East NSW and Tablelands: burned grazing land vs livestock and farm business change (SA2/SA4 before-after)
test_ideas.indicator_strengthened: DL (livestock, farm assets and land burned per council) and the agriculture part of IL
test_ideas.data: NSW FESM 2019-20 severity raster; NSW Landuse 2017 v1.5; ABS Agricultural Commodities 2015-16 and 2020-21 (SA2/LGA) and 2018-19 to 2019-20 (SA4); ABS Census agricultural businesses
test_ideas.fire_matching: Overlay FESM burned area on Landuse polygons coded grazing, cropping and horticulture to get hectares of farmland burned per SA2 (fire x location). Compare change in livestock head and agricultural businesses between 2015-16 and 2020-21 at SA2 against the share of farmland burned; at SA4 use annual 2018-19 vs 2019-20 stock counts for quick before-after.
test_ideas.gap_filling: Estimate livestock lost = burned grazing hectares x stocking rate from the unburned SA2's own 2015-16 stock per hectare; show it next to the survey's state totals (about 56,000 killed or euthanised in the literature) as a plausibility check. Flag that 2020-21 stock reflects restocking and drought breaking.
test_ideas.expected_direction: Fewer livestock per hectare and fewer agricultural businesses in SA2s with more burned farmland, with the stock effect larger than the business-count effect (Experiment 7 found no sector business effect on agriculture, so the stock test is the more sensitive one).
test_ideas.files_and_sizes: ABS 2020-21 SA2 xlsx 1.33 MB; ABS 2019-20 SA4 csv 1.24 MB; Landuse zip (size unconfirmed, likely hundreds of MB); FESM raster zip (size unconfirmed, likely hundreds of MB to GB; could instead use the burned-extent polygons already in the project and skip FESM). Also needs ABS 2015-16 agricultural SA2 file (not confirmed in this session).
test_ideas.risks: 2015-16 vs 2020-21 gap includes the 2018-19 drought and later restocking; farm numbers shift for non-fire reasons; ABS cut-off of A$40,000 excludes small holdings; stock counts are at 30 June only; need to check ASGS edition mismatch between 2016 and 2021 SA2s.

test_ideas.title: Where the lost earners worked: workplace jobs by industry inside the fire zone, with forest-loss exposure
test_ideas.indicator_strengthened: IL: jobs and wage income at workplaces inside or near the fire outline, by industry (forestry, farm, accommodation); also splits the detected SA2 total-income fall (-1.6% per 10pp) into who and where
test_ideas.data: ABS Jobs in Australia (employee jobs and wages by industry x SA2, place of work); ABS Census 2016 vs 2021 destination-zone workplace population; NSW FESM burn extent and severity; forest/plantation tenure layer (ABARES National Forest Inventory / Forestry Corporation estate) to count forest area burned per SA2
test_ideas.fire_matching: Space: give each SA2 the share of homes inside a fire outline (the Exp 7 estimate) plus, for forestry, the share of its plantation/forest land burned (FESM x tenure). Time: year 0 is the financial year of the fire (Black Summer = 2019-20); compare years 0 to +3 with the pre-fire year and with matched SA2s of the same industry mix but no fire. For tourism, sanity-check the Mar-2020 quarter in TRA tourism-region data.
test_ideas.gap_filling: Data do not say how much of a mill's log supply burned, so estimate it as burned plantation/forest hectares in the SA2 divided by total hectares (transparent, like homes-inside-fire). Suppressed industry cells in small SA2s are dropped, not filled; report how many.
test_ideas.expected_direction: Forestry and wood-product jobs fall in SA2s with a high share of forest burned (Snowy Valleys, Bega); accommodation jobs fall in the Dec-Mar quarter only; agriculture jobs fall slowly; construction and health jobs may rise as an offset. Given Exp 7, many sectors may still show no detectable effect above the stated bound, so report bounds.
test_ideas.files_and_sizes: ABS Jobs in Australia SA2 x industry cubes (~20-60 MB, 2011-12 to latest); ABS Census 2016 and 2021 Place of Work DataPacks for NSW (~100-300 MB); NSW FESM 2019-20 (~100s MB to 1 GB); forest tenure or NFI forest cover for NSW (~100-500 MB). Approximate; not confirmed. No download made.
test_ideas.risks: Industry cells are suppressed in small SA2s; forestry may sit in only 3-5 SA2s, so power is low and the answer may be 'cannot tell'. 2021 Census includes COVID effects. Place-of-work changes can reflect a mill closing for reasons other than fire. Needs a pre-registered rule file like earlier experiments.

test_ideas.title: Monthly rebuilding and building-approvals response after each fire (the offset side of IL)
test_ideas.indicator_strengthened: IL: net vs gross indirect loss (construction jobs as an offset), and the link between destroyed homes (DL) and local labour demand; also tests whether rebuild activity happens where housing was lost
test_ideas.data: ABS Building Approvals SA2 monthly cubes; NSW Planning Portal development application open data (lodgement date, address); NSW Fair Trading rental bond lodgements by postcode and month; NSW Reconstruction Authority rebuild counts
test_ideas.fire_matching: Align each SA2 on its own month 0 = the month the fire was declared out (or peak destruction). Count approvals and DAs in months -12 to +36 relative to month 0 and compare with matched SA2s with no fire, using homes-inside-fire as the dose. Rental bond lodgements by postcode (monthly) give a rent-pressure series over the same window.
test_ideas.gap_filling: Destroyed homes per SA2 come from existing DL work (homes inside fire estimate, or Reconstruction Authority counts). If DA addresses cannot be matched to burned lots, estimate rebuild share as new-dwelling DAs divided by homes destroyed in the SA2 (flag the assumption). Rental bond data may start after 2020, so use Black Summer only if older files are found; otherwise use later fires.
test_ideas.expected_direction: Building approvals rise above control SA2s 6-24 months after the fire in proportion to homes destroyed (a rebuild surge); rents rise in small towns with many destroyed homes. Exp 7 found no construction-income response at annual SA2 level, so a monthly approvals signal would be new information rather than a repeat.
test_ideas.files_and_sizes: ABS Building Approvals SA2 monthly cubes for NSW (~10-30 MB); NSW Planning Portal DA open data extract (~100s MB, API key needed); NSW Fair Trading rental bond lodgement files (~0.6-25 MB each, many months). Approximate; no download made.
test_ideas.risks: Approvals measure intent, not completed work; rebuilds lag and many owners do not rebuild (Mallacoota 15 of 120). Insurance and builder shortages delay DAs. DA data availability and field names must be checked; rental bond history before 2021 may not be online. The API key is an account step for Ray, not me.

test_ideas.title: Grant timing and size vs homes lost, by fire and council, with a 'who got money first' check
test_ideas.indicator_strengthened: FP (grants and cost shifting). It gives the existing FP indicator a timing side (months to money) and a fairness side (grant per home lost), where Experiment 7 only used one annual number.
test_ideas.data: OLG time series (already in hand) for annual grants per resident, plus a hand-built list of BLER, BCRRF and Black Summer Bushfire Recovery grant awards by council from GrantConnect award pages and NSW Reconstruction Authority evaluation reports. NEMA DRFA activation dates by LGA mark when each council could claim. Homes destroyed per 1,000 dwellings from the existing panel.
test_ideas.fire_matching: Take each council x fire row (fire footprint and ignition date). Count grant money awarded in the 12 months after the fire's end date versus months 13-36. Compare councils with the same fire size but different homes lost, using the existing homes-destroyed-per-1,000 measure. For the political side, compare grant per home lost across the first-round and later rounds, as a descriptive table only.
test_ideas.gap_filling: Where GrantConnect gives only the Commonwealth side, use the NSW Audit Office report totals (A$541.8m BLER) to scale council shares; where a council has no project dates, assume payment in the council's financial year of announcement. Mark all filled values so they can be dropped in a sensitivity check.
test_ideas.expected_direction: Grant per home lost should fall as homes lost rise in late rounds if allocation is not matched to need (worse = fairness gap), and annual grants should rise in the year after the fire, as Experiment 7 already found. A timing lag of 12 months or more is expected.
test_ideas.files_and_sizes: No new bulk download needed for the first step: OLG time series already in the project. New: GrantConnect award pages for the Black Summer Bushfire Recovery Grants (web records, number unknown), NSW Reconstruction Authority evaluation PDFs (BLER Stage 1 3.69 MB, BLER Stage 2 and BIRP Stream 2 9.61 MB, BIRP Stream 1 3.96 MB, BCRRF Phase 1 3.93 MB, summary 1.07 MB; about 22 MB total), NEMA DRFA activation history (small), Location-Based Disaster Assistance Payments (small).
test_ideas.risks: I have not opened the PDFs, so council-level tables inside them are unverified. GrantConnect bulk export is unverified; hand collection may be needed. About half of grant dollars go to infrastructure and business, so grant per home lost is a rough measure. NSW data portal pages for DRFA/payments blocked my fetch (403), so check access first.

test_ideas.title: Property sales price and rate-base change near fires, using postcode sale dates
test_ideas.indicator_strengthened: FP (council rate base) and SL (household wealth). Rateable land value is a council revenue variable and sale price is a household wealth variable; neither is in Bowen's current Y.
test_ideas.data: NSW Valuer General Bulk Property Sales Information (free, sale-by-sale with postcode and date) and Bulk Land Value CSVs (one per LGA, July 2017 on). Fire footprints and homes-inside-fire estimate from the existing panel.
test_ideas.fire_matching: For each postcode (or SA2) intersecting a fire footprint, take median sale price per quarter for 8 quarters before and 12 quarters after the fire end date, and compare with postcodes in the same LGA outside the footprint (a within-council control). For rate base, compare 1 July land values the year before and the year after, by LGA, against councils without fires.
test_ideas.gap_filling: Postcodes with fewer than about 5 sales in a quarter get a pooled half-year median. Postcode-to-fire overlap uses the same 'homes inside fire outline' share as Experiment 7. Sales in the fire footprint after 2019 are mixed with COVID-era regional price rises, so use same-LGA unburned postcodes as the baseline and flag the ambiguity.
test_ideas.expected_direction: Mixed, as the mechanism says: small dip in prices in the first one or two quarters in burned postcodes, then catch-up or overshoot after rebuild; rate base probably flat or slightly up at council level. A null above a stated bound is a plausible result.
test_ideas.files_and_sizes: PSI weekly/annual DAT zip files for NSW from 2015 to 2025 (size not shown on the pages I saw; probably a few GB total, so download only the years and LGAs needed); Bulk Land Value zip (one CSV per LGA, July 2017 to 2025, likely 100s of MB). Request approval before any download.
test_ideas.risks: Free PSI licence is non-commercial only, which should be fine for a school project but should be stated. Few sales in burned postcodes right after fires (the Mallacoota listings example fell from 84 to 20). Land value files are annual and valuing dates are the 1 July; fire timing within the year is lost. COVID regional boom is a strong confounder, as in Experiment 7 rents.

test_ideas.title: Domestic assault after fire: monthly event study by suburb/postcode (BOCSAR)
test_ideas.indicator_strengthened: SL: add a domestic-violence-per-1,000 indicator to the Social Loss pillar (monthly), and a new tier-level SL measure that is not a household-income proxy
test_ideas.data: BOCSAR suburb (or postcode) monthly counts of domestic violence related assault, with non-domestic assault as a control offence; ABS ERP by SA2 mapped to postcode for per-1,000 rates; Experiment 7 'homes inside fire outline' share per postcode as exposure.
test_ideas.fire_matching: For each fire (footprint x ignition date), mark each postcode with a share of dwellings inside or within 1 km of the outline (Experiment 7 method). Take 12 months before to 24 months after, in months relative to the fire. Compare against unburned postcodes in the same LGA/region over the same calendar months. Run placebo with fire dates shifted 3 years earlier. Use all NSW fires 2013-2022, not just Black Summer, to avoid the covid lockdown (from March 2020) swamping a single season.
test_ideas.gap_filling: Small monthly counts: pool postcodes into exposure bands (0, <10%, 10-30%, >30% of dwellings near fire) and use 3-month windows, estimating rates with a count model (Poisson/negative binomial with area and month effects). Population denominator comes from SA2 ERP by area weights; any postcode with missing months is treated as zero counts only if the BOCSAR file lists it with zeros. Say clearly that DV is under-reported.
test_ideas.expected_direction: Increase in DV assault rate in heavily affected postcodes, about 6 to 24 months after the fire (literature: stress, housing loss, alcohol); weaker or negative in the first month when services are cut off. Non-domestic assault should rise less. Per Experiment 7 rules, report as 'no detectable increase above X per 1,000' if the interval includes zero.
test_ideas.files_and_sizes: BOCSAR SuburbData.zip (size not stated on pages seen; likely tens of MB; check before download) or the postcode dataset on https://data.nsw.gov.au/data/en/dataset/crime-data-by-offence; ABS SA2 population file already in project (688 KB); ABS postcode-SA2 correspondence (small); fire footprints and Experiment 7 exposure table already in project. No other download needed.
test_ideas.risks: Counts are small and DV is under-reported; fire-hit towns are small so power is low; covid lockdown overlaps Black Summer; evacuations and population change move denominators; BOCSAR page returned 403 in my check so file layout is unconfirmed. Treat a null as 'cannot tell' unless the confidence band is tight.

test_ideas.title: Rents and rebuilding at postcode/SA2 monthly scale (rental bonds plus building approvals)
test_ideas.indicator_strengthened: SL (housing/displacement indicator: median new-bond rent change and rebuild rate) and X (rental market tightness as a moderator). Complements Experiment 7's council-level rent null, which could have been diluted at council scale.
test_ideas.data: NSW Fair Trading rental bond lodgements by postcode (weekly rent, bedrooms, count of new bonds); ABS monthly Building Approvals by SA2 (dwelling units); Census 2016 and 2021 dwelling counts per SA1/SA2 as a cross-check; Experiment 7 homes-destroyed and homes-inside-fire shares.
test_ideas.fire_matching: For each fire, build a postcode-month panel (SA2-month for approvals): outcome = median new-bond weekly rent for 2-bedroom units (and number of new bonds as a supply/turnover signal); exposure = homes destroyed per 1,000 dwellings (or share inside fire). Event windows: 6 months before to 36 months after the fire date. Controls: unburned postcodes within the same regional market (same LGA group or SA4), same calendar months, to absorb the covid regional rent boom. For rebuilding, cumulative approved dwellings after the fire divided by homes destroyed, by month, in burned SA2s versus the same ratio in unburned SA2s.
test_ideas.gap_filling: Postcodes with few bonds in a month: use rolling 3-month medians and drop cells under 10 bonds. Convert Experiment 7's SA2/mesh-block exposure to postcode with area/dwelling weights. Approvals are not completions: report 'approvals per destroyed home' as a ceiling on the rebuilt share and add the Census 2016-to-2021 net dwelling change as a second estimate (both transparent estimates).
test_ideas.expected_direction: Rent: up in high-loss postcodes within 6 to 18 months (strongest where more than about 5-10% of homes were lost), fading later; falling new-bond counts if stock was lost. Rebuilding: approvals rise in burned SA2s but well below 1 per destroyed home for several years (news reports about 50 of 464 rebuilt in Bega Valley after 5 years). If still null at postcode level, that confirms the council-level null and the 'losses were absorbed by insurers/government' reading.
test_ideas.files_and_sizes: Rental bond files from https://www.nsw.gov.au/housing-and-construction/rental-forms-surveys-and-data/rental-bond-data: monthly lodgements about 0.6-0.8 MB each (2022-2026) and annual lodgements 6.8-8.3 MB (2021-2025); 2016-2021 months need archived files (check data.nsw.gov.au listing first). ABS building approvals SA2 monthly CSVs from https://data.gov.au/data/dataset/475e832b-1a7b-4398-ba25-dd356ff91dc2 (small each; about 60-120 months needed). Optional Census DataPack NSW SA2 2016 and 2021 (size not stated; all-Australia GCP up to 584 MB, NSW much less).
test_ideas.risks: Bonds only cover new tenancies and miss holiday lets; covid regional rent boom (2020-22) overlaps and the control group may be affected too; pre-2022 monthly files may be hard to find; approvals include non-rebuild construction; small postcodes give noisy medians. Note this is partly a re-cut of Experiment 7 Day 10 rents, so its value is the finer scale, not new data type.

missing_mechanisms.name: Deaths and injuries (human capital lost)
missing_mechanisms.why: Bowen's DL explicitly includes deaths/injuries (26 NSW deaths in Black Summer, burn admissions in AIHW gov-13) but no mechanism row carries them; needed so DL is complete for the severity tiers.

missing_mechanisms.name: Public infrastructure and council asset damage (roads, bridges, water/sewer, halls)
missing_mechanisms.why: DL in Bowen's framework includes infrastructure; the table only mentions it inside M40/M41 as a council budget item. DRFA Category B restoration claims and OLG asset write-downs/renewal spending would measure it per council.

missing_mechanisms.name: Destroyed homes owned by non-residents (holiday and second homes) - loss falls outside the local resident population
missing_mechanisms.why: On the South Coast a large share of destroyed dwellings were holiday homes (news-10: 27% of Batemans Bay stock vacant year-round). This is a direct candidate explanation for Experiment 7's resident-income nulls, and Census 2016 unoccupied-dwelling share by SA1/SA2 is open and small. It should be an X variable in the RF and a moderator of the DL -> IL/SL link.

missing_mechanisms.name: Insurance payouts as a local money inflow
missing_mechanisms.pillar: Moderator (offsets DL -> SL; also part of IL offset with M14)
missing_mechanisms.why: Experiment 7 already used insured losses (about A$2.3bn) as one reason local income looked normal, but the table treats insurance only as a shortfall (M21). Payouts that replace lost wealth and pay local builders are a separate cushioning mechanism.

missing_mechanisms.name: Concurrent drought (2017-2020) amplifying farm loss and confounding farm outcomes
missing_mechanisms.pillar: X (moderator on DL farm / IL farm)
missing_mechanisms.why: Several records (survey-29, news-32, M02 text) say drought compounded fire loss, but M44 only covers later shocks (COVID, floods, mice). Drought severity before the fire (BoM rainfall deciles, open) is needed as an X variable or any farm test is confounded.

missing_mechanisms.name: Government-funded clean-up and debris removal
missing_mechanisms.why: NSW and the Commonwealth paid for property clean-up (A$75m joint clean-up in gov-44; demolition up to A$100,000 per site in news-52). It is a large, visible fiscal cost per destroyed home and is not its own row.

missing_mechanisms.name: Park, forest and road closures cutting nature-based tourism for months
missing_mechanisms.why: National parks and state forests stayed closed long after the flames (parks are the draw for South Coast and Snowy tourism). This makes IL last longer than the evacuation weeks in M06, and closure days per council could be an IL driver.

missing_mechanisms.name: Aboriginal cultural and Country loss
missing_mechanisms.why: gov-25 notes high distress among Aboriginal people, but M33 treats Indigenous status only as a disadvantage moderator. Loss of cultural sites and Country is a separate social loss named in the Royal Commission. Low measurability, so note it rather than test it.

missing_mechanisms.name: Bank hardship deferrals and credit relief
missing_mechanisms.why: Banks offered mortgage deferrals after the fires (then COVID deferrals). This hides financial stress in arrears data for 6-12 months, so it affects how any M18 hardship test should be timed.

pillar_fixes.new_pillar: SL (household wealth), with only a secondary FP note
pillar_fixes.why: NSW council rate income is capped by the IPART rate peg. Changes in land value move the rate burden between ratepayers rather than changing council revenue, so the FP channel is weak. The test idea itself admits house prices are not in Bowen's current Y, so as framed it drifts from the framework.

pillar_fixes.new_pillar: IL (lost labour time and earnings), with the compensation payments under FP
pillar_fixes.why: Volunteer days away from paid work are lost labour input and earnings (A$143.5m paid plus A$116.5m unpaid leave), which is an economic flow loss rather than a wellbeing loss.

pillar_fixes.new_pillar: SL for the health outcome, but smoke exposure itself should be added as an X variable (fire physics group)
pillar_fixes.why: M05, M11 and M32 all need smoke days, an exposure that is different from burned area. Putting smoke days per council-fire in X keeps it inside Bowen's framework, so it does not become a separate smoke project.

pillar_fixes.new_pillar: X variable (count of declared disasters before and after each fire per LGA)
pillar_fixes.why: It works as a covariate or moderator in the council x fire RF, not as a Y component. Tagging it as X makes that clear.

pillar_fixes.new_pillar: FP (public spending), with a moderator role on SL
pillar_fixes.why: Disaster payments per capita by LGA are a direct fiscal cost and belong in FP. Their cushioning effect on SL is secondary.

pillar_fixes.new_pillar: SL, but flag that it is not testable at area level
pillar_fixes.why: Movers versus stayers needs linked individual data (ABS ACLD or ATO, both restricted). Area population change only measures the area, not the movers, so the pillar note should not promise a household-level indicator.

unsupported_claims.problem: Checked The Conversation (news-33). The +1.3 pp rise in nil/negative-income households applies to economically disadvantaged peri-urban areas with severe burn, not to severely burned communities in general. The study is a Census 2016-2021 comparison and the article mentions no COVID control. The table should state that subgroup and the COVID caveat.

The rent figures (+A$20/10%, +A$26/13%) are confirmed in news-33, but they come from the same 2016-2021 Census design that overlaps the COVID regional rent boom. Experiment 7 found no detectable council-level rent effect. 'Strong' should be 'moderate', with the confound stated.

Checked SBS (news-1). 'About 50 of 464 Bega Valley homes rebuilt' is a claim by an advocacy group founder (Social Justice Advocates of the Sapphire Coast), not an official count. Label it as an advocate estimate. The 'strong' rating rests mostly on first-person accounts.

lit-20 (PreventionWeb) returned 403 so the '~7 times' figure could not be verified. It comes from Black Saturday (Victoria) research, not NSW Black Summer. news-48, news-49 and survey-46 are warnings, not measurements, and survey-58 is anecdotal. Evidence for Black Summer NSW should be 'moderate', and the table should say no measured NSW Black Summer increase was found.
It mixes NSW and national figures. A$1.88bn is the NSW insurance cost (AIDR), while 38,181 claims and A$2.32bn are national ICA totals. State which is which.

The livestock counts conflict: over 56,000 (lit-30, Cowled, south-eastern Australia), over 100,000 (gov-58/survey-27, WWF modelling) and 6,284 in NSW (survey-29, early DPI count). The A$4-5bn figure is a modelled WWF/USyd estimate. Report the range and the geography of each number.

The 61% spillover and 7,300 jobs come from an input-output model (Reiner et al.), not observed data, and input-output models tend to overstate flow-on effects. gov-4 (Deloitte) notes that spending partly moves to other regions, so local and national net losses differ. 'Strong' should be 'moderate (modelled)'.

Spot-checked AIDR (lit-6). The sector numbers (agriculture -31%, retail -13%, tourism -12%, health +8%) are confirmed. The page summary gave employed people -8%, while the ~10% headline comes from the Deakin media release. All of these are Victoria 2009, Census 2006-2011. The Maui figures are US. Say 'not NSW' in the evidence column.

The 1.8 million missed-work figure is from an Australia Institute online poll (an advocacy organisation, extrapolated to the population). The per-smoke-day earnings effect is from US data. Flag it as indicative only.

'ESL and taxes over 50% of NSW premiums' is an Insurance Council claim relayed by survey-9, and the record itself notes a conflicting 70% figure. It is an industry advocacy number and should not stand as evidence without a primary source.

The '~48% of A$2.74b delivered' figure (news-55) comes from an advocacy-commissioned report, and news-56 shows the government disputed it (A$1.9b claimed). Present both. The political-allocation claim is well supported by the Audit Office (gov-30).
'Kinglake +150% in 10 years' is an agent or analyst comment with no comparison area, and the Mallacoota listings are anecdotal. The only systematic evidence is from California (FRBSF).

Confirmed in lit-7 (low-income -18%, women -14% vs men -9%, renters -14%). However, Experiment 7 found that the Experiment 6 claim that disadvantage raises Y vanished under the placebo check. The table should say Australian support for amplification is from Black Saturday individual data, and that Experiment 7's area-level data did not reproduce it.

data_problems: ABS Jobs in Australia is mapped as 'place of work' in M04, M06, M12 and M14. As far as I know, its regional data are coded to the job holder's residential address (from tax records), so it does NOT show jobs located inside the fire zone. Verify on the ABS methodology page before relying on it. Workplace counts need Census Place of Work (destination zone), which is only available for 2016 and 2021.

Jobs in Australia SA2 x detailed industry (forestry/logging, wood products) is likely unavailable or heavily suppressed. Industry detail is mostly at division level. The forestry test (M04) may fail on the data alone.

Rental bond data descriptions contradict each other. M19 and M44 say monthly files only from 2022, while M43 says '1990s to current'. Experiment 7 already built council-level rents from this source, so the historic postcode-month file exists in the project or an archive. Check the Experiment 7 panels folder before any download.

Building approvals SA2 coverage is described inconsistently. M20 says monthly SA2 is about 2011 onward, while M43 says SA2 is only for some past releases. ABS does publish SA2 monthly approvals (data cubes and the ABS Data API); confirm the series and boundary edition (ASGS 2016 vs 2021).

Value of Agricultural Commodities SA2 file sizes conflict: 1.33 MB in the M02 entry versus 5-20 MB in M03. Only census years (2015-16, 2020-21) have SA2 detail, and 2015-16 is pre-drought while 2020-21 is post-drought restocking, so a fire effect cannot be separated from drought.

Several datasets are paid, restricted or need an account and should not be counted as available open data: Spendmapp (paid), Climate Valuation (paid), Services Australia monthly small-area MBS (cost recovery), HILDA (application), ACARA NAPLAN extract (application), ICA postcode claims (member only), NSW DPI damage survey (request), RFS evacuation archive (request), distributor outage data (request). TableBuilder, AURIN and the NSW Planning Portal API need accounts that Ray must create himself.

AIHW Medicare mental-health data are annual by SA3 and change with COVID telehealth from March 2020. That is too coarse to match to a fire, so M23 and M24 are not testable at fine scale with open data.
HealthStats NSW ED data are at Local Health District level, much coarser than council, so they cannot be matched to council x fire rows.

Several entries carry fetch failures (403) and the details came from search summaries only: NEMA disaster-payments-by-LGA, DRFA activation history, BOCSAR SuburbData, RAA declarations, ACMA report. The NEMA payment series reportedly starts in 2020, so whether Black Summer is covered is unconfirmed.

The DSS URL in the M35 entry is mislabelled (it points to a Services Australia listing). DSS SA2 data have rounding and method changes from Dec 2022 and a COVID JobSeeker surge in 2020. Both are already known from Experiment 7 and affect any re-cut.

Census 2021 is post-fire and mid-COVID (lockdowns in NSW in August 2021). Every '2016 vs 2021' design (M15, M16, M17, M20, M28, M34) mixes the fire with COVID and the regional move boom. Use 2016 only as a fixed pre-fire weight or moderator.
The FESM raster size is unconfirmed (could be over 1 GB). The project already has burned-extent polygons, so FESM is only needed if burn severity is essential. Prefer the existing outlines.
The TRA LGA profiles are pooled multi-year survey averages, and the tourism-region quarterly series covers about 12 large NSW regions. Neither gives fire-matched quarterly visitor data for a council.
critic.framework_fit:
The table mostly enriches Bowen's framework rather than replacing it. All 45 mechanisms carry a DL/IL/FP/SL, X or moderator tag, and most map to a council-level indicator that can be added to the council x fire panel. The table's most useful contributions are:
(a) an explicit FP 'who pays' block (M37-M42) that gives FP more than one annual grant number;
(b) moderators and X variables (M21, M33, M44, M45, plus the suggested smoke days and holiday-home share) that can go straight into the RF as X and into the severity tiers and risk map;
(c) SL indicators that are not income proxies (domestic violence, rebuild rate, rent), which matter because Experiment 7 found income-type outcomes mostly flat.

Points of drift to watch:
1. Smoke (M05, M11, M32) is a new exposure dimension. It must enter as an X variable (smoke days per council-fire), not become a separate smoke-health study.
2. Property prices (M43) are pitched as 'not in Bowen's Y'. Either attach them to SL household wealth or drop them.
3. M16, M24, M25 and M26 need individual-level or restricted survey data and cannot produce council x fire rows. Keep them as literature context only.
4. Much of the 'strong' evidence comes from Victoria 2009, the US or Maui, so the table should state that it may not transfer to NSW council aggregates.
5. Tests must be sharper than Experiment 7: monthly timing, a targeted outcome, or a better-placed population. They should output an indicator that can be aggregated back to council x fire rows so it plugs into Y and the RF. Repeat annual SA2 or council income tests should be excluded.

The missing 'non-resident owned homes' mechanism matters most for framework fit. It gives a principled X variable that explains why DL (which tracks fire size) does not pass through to resident IL/SL. That would strengthen the pre-fire risk map and severity tiers rather than undermining them.

best_tests.title: Domestic violence assault after fire: monthly council x fire event study (BOCSAR), with non-domestic assault as a control offence
best_tests.pillar_indicator: SL: new indicator 'domestic-violence-related assaults per 1,000 residents' (council x fire row: change over months +6 to +24 compared with months -24 to -1)
best_tests.data: BOCSAR recorded crime by LGA, monthly counts by offence (RCI_offencebymonth file, 1995 onward), with the suburb file as an optional finer cut. ABS ERP population (already in project). Council x fire panel fire dates and homes-destroyed per 1,000 (already in project).
best_tests.fire_matching: Use every fire in the existing NSW 2015-2025 council x fire panel, not just Black Summer, so the COVID lockdown from March 2020 does not dominate. Month 0 is the fire month. Windows run from 24 months before to 24 months after. Exposure is the existing homes destroyed per 1,000 dwellings (or residents affected share). Comparison is unburned councils in the same months (calendar-month effects) plus each council's own seasonality. The outcome is DV assault minus non-domestic assault, as a rate or as a ratio of the two, which nets out general policing and reporting changes. Placebo: shift fire dates back 3 years. Optional finer step: suburbs inside versus outside the outline within the same council.
best_tests.gap_filling: Little is needed because BOCSAR publishes full monthly counts with zeros. Pool months into 3-month windows for small councils and use a count model with council and month effects. Interpolate the population denominator between June ERP values (a stated rule).
best_tests.expected_direction: A higher DV assault rate in councils with more homes destroyed, appearing about 6-24 months after the fire. It may dip in months 0-2 when services and roads are cut. Non-domestic assault should rise less. If the interval includes zero, report 'no detectable increase above X per 1,000'. Under-reporting means a null is a lower bound, not proof of no effect.
best_tests.files_and_sizes: BOCSAR RCI_offencebymonth.xlsm (LGA x offence x month, size not confirmed, likely about 5-30 MB). Optional: BOCSAR SuburbData.zip (size not confirmed, likely tens of MB). Both are from bocsar.nsw.gov.au / data.nsw.gov.au 'crime-data-by-offence'. Nothing else new. Needs Ray's OK before download.
best_tests.why_this_one: It is untested by Experiment 7. It uses open, small, monthly data published at exactly the council geography of Bowen's panel. It covers many fires, not one season, which helps with power and COVID. The direction is clear and the control-offence design is strong. It adds an SL indicator that is not a household-income proxy, which is where Experiment 7 kept finding nothing.
best_tests.main_risk: DV is under-reported, and fires disrupt policing and reporting (which could bias the result downward). Small rural councils give noisy counts. Most of the large-loss rows are still Black Summer, which overlaps COVID. The BOCSAR file layout is unconfirmed (my fetch hit a 404 or 403 page).

best_tests.title: Rebuild gap: monthly dwelling approvals per destroyed home in burned SA2s (plus postcode-month new-bond rents as a second outcome)
best_tests.pillar_indicator: SL: 'share of destroyed homes with a rebuild approval after 12/24/36 months' (displacement/housing indicator), aggregated to council x fire rows. It also tests the DL -> SL pass-through and the IL rebuild offset.
best_tests.data: ABS Building Approvals by SA2, monthly (new houses and dwelling units). Experiment 7's SA2 homes-inside-fire dose and council homes destroyed (in project). Experiment 7's existing NSW Fair Trading bond lodgement file, re-cut to postcode-month (check whether it is already in project before any download).
best_tests.fire_matching: For each fire, burned SA2s are matched to month 0 = fire month. Count approved new houses over months -24 to +48. The outcome is cumulative excess approvals (compared with each SA2's own pre-fire monthly average and with unburned SA2s in the same SA4 over the same months) divided by estimated homes destroyed in that SA2. Rents: postcode-month median new-bond rent and bond counts over months -12 to +36, compared with unburned postcodes in the same SA4.
best_tests.gap_filling: Homes destroyed per SA2 come from Experiment 7's homes-inside-fire estimate scaled to the RFS council total (already a stated rule). Approvals include non-rebuild builds, so the ratio is an upper bound on the rebuilt share. Postcode-months with fewer than 10 bonds use rolling 3-month medians or are dropped.
best_tests.expected_direction: Excess approvals rise from about month 6 but stay well below 1 per destroyed home by month 36 (news reports suggest well under half). They are slower in SA2s with lower SEIFA or more underinsurance risk (M21/M33 moderator). Rents rise within 6-18 months only in small postcodes with high loss.
best_tests.files_and_sizes: ABS Building Approvals SA2 monthly (data cube or ABS Data API CSV for NSW, about 5-30 MB, unconfirmed; check ASGS 2016 vs 2021 edition). Rental bonds: first check the Experiment 7 panels folder; if the postcode-month history is missing, NSW Fair Trading annual lodgement files are about 7-8 MB per year (2019-2023, about 40 MB). Needs Ray's OK.
best_tests.why_this_one: It is untested: Experiment 7 measured homes destroyed and construction-sector income, never rebuilding. The data are monthly, at SA2 scale, open, and modest in size. The direction is clear. It turns the one robust DL signal into a time-to-recovery measure that can feed severity tiers (how long a council stays damaged) and the SL pillar.
best_tests.main_risk: Approvals measure intent, not completion. Holiday-home owners who choose not to rebuild look like 'displacement' when they are not. The 2021-22 construction cost surge and the HomeBuilder grant (COVID) boosted approvals everywhere, so the comparison group must absorb this. SA2 boundary edition changes.

best_tests.title: Who carries the detected earner loss: holiday-home share and tourism dependence as moderators of the SA2 total-income fall
best_tests.pillar_indicator: X variables for the RF and risk map: pre-fire non-resident (unoccupied) dwelling share, accommodation/food employment share, SEIFA 2016. They act as moderators of the IL/SL pass-through from DL.
best_tests.data: Census 2016 General Community Profile for NSW SA2 (dwelling occupancy / unoccupied dwellings; industry of employment; tenure). SEIFA 2016 SA2. Experiment 7's SA2 PIA total income and earners panel and homes-inside-fire dose (already in project).
best_tests.fire_matching: Rerun the Experiment 7 Day 9 design unchanged (SA2 x year, dose = share of homes inside the fire outline, same year effects and future-fire placebo), adding pre-specified interactions of dose with (a) 2016 unoccupied-dwelling share above or below the median, (b) accommodation/food share in the top tercile, and (c) fire reaching the SA2 in Dec-Jan. The outcome is income earners and total income at year 2, which were the detected outcomes.
best_tests.gap_filling: None. The 2016 shares are fixed pre-fire weights. For an SA2 with several fires, the timing rule is the earliest fire covering more than 10% of homes.
best_tests.expected_direction: A larger fall in earners in high-tourism SA2s and Christmas-peak fires. A smaller resident-income effect per home destroyed where many destroyed homes were holiday homes, because the loss falls on non-residents. That supports a non-resident-share X variable in the RF.
best_tests.files_and_sizes: ABS Census 2016 GCP DataPack, NSW SA2 (about 15-30 MB zip, unconfirmed). ABS SEIFA 2016 SA2 xlsx (about 1-2 MB). Everything else is already in the Experiment 7 project. Needs Ray's OK.
best_tests.why_this_one: It is the cheapest test and builds directly on Experiment 7's only detected income result, splitting it rather than repeating it. Unlike the other ideas it produces X variables that slot straight into Bowen's RF, severity tiers and pre-fire risk map. The holiday-home share is a concrete explanation for the DL-tracks-fire but income-flat pattern.
best_tests.main_risk: There are only about 57-72 treated SA2s, essentially one season, so interaction estimates will be imprecise and may end as 'cannot tell'; report the bounds. Tourism share is correlated with coastal location and COVID border effects in 2020-21. Industry is by residence, not workplace.
